knowledge_statements.title: Stochastic Subgradient Oracles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unbiased stochastic generalized-gradient oracle with controlled second moment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^d\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper and locally Lipschitz on an open set \(U\). A stochastic subgradient oracle on \(U\) is a measurable mapping \(G:U\times\Omega\to\mathbb{R}^d\) such that, for every \(x\in U\),
\[\mathbb{E}[G(x,\xi)]\in\partial f(x),\qquad \mathbb{E}[\lVert G(x,\xi)\rVert^2]\leq M(x)^2<+\infty.\]
Here \(\partial f(x)\) is the chosen generalized subdifferential and \(M\) is a deterministic moment bound. A globally bounded oracle uses \(M(x)\leq M\) on \(U\); a local-growth oracle instead permits a specified state-dependent bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A stochastic subgradient oracle returns a measurable random vector whose expectation is a generalized subgradient and whose second moment is controlled.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper and locally Lipschitz on an open set \(U\).
\(G(x,\xi)\) is measurable and integrable for every \(x\in U\).
The stated second-moment bound is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb{E}[G(x,\xi)]\in\partial f(x)\) and \(\mathbb{E}\lVert G(x,\xi)\rVert^2\leq M(x)^2\) for every \(x\in U\).

notation.meaning: random oracle output at the query point

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The oracle definition depends materially on the generalized-subdifferential and unbiasedness conventions, while the probability space, random element, and measurability structure associated with Omega and xi are not introduced. An authoritative stochastic weakly convex optimization source is required before choosing the correct formulation.

assumptions_latex: For almost every \(\xi\), \(c(\cdot,\xi)\) is differentiable and \(h(\cdot,\xi)\) is proper and subdifferentiable at \(c(x,\xi)\).
The regularizer \(r\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and has a computable proximal map.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(G(x,\xi)=J_c(x,\xi)^{\mathsf T}v(x,\xi)\) is the sample composite first-order estimate supplied by the oracle.

notation.meaning: Sample inner map and its Jacobian.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional smooth-inner, nonsmooth-outer composite oracle with a proximable regularizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(F(x)=\mathbb{E}[h(c(x,\xi),\xi)]+r(x)\). A composite first-order oracle queried at \(x\) draws \(\xi\) and returns \(c(x,\xi)\), its Jacobian \(J_c(x,\xi)\), and a vector \(v(x,\xi)\in\partial h(c(x,\xi),\xi)\). It thereby supplies \(G(x,\xi)=J_c(x,\xi)^{\mathsf T}v(x,\xi)\), together with access to \(\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda r}(z)=\arg\min_y\{r(y)+(2\lambda)^{-1}\|y-z\|^2\}\) for admissible \(\lambda>0\). The definition specifies the returned information; unbiasedness or moment bounds require separate assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A composite oracle samples the inner map, its Jacobian, and an outer subgradient, producing a chain-rule estimate while exposing the regularizer's proximal map.
knowledge_statements.title: Composite First-Order Oracles

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No inspectable citation supports this particular composite-oracle interface. The codomain of c and domain of h are also unspecified, so the dimensions of the Jacobian and outer subgradient are not fully introduced.

assumptions_latex: The sample loss \(f(\cdot,\xi)\) is proper and lower semicontinuous.
The displayed proximal subproblem has at least one minimizer almost surely.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The oracle output belongs to \(\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda f(\cdot,\xi)}(x)\) almost surely.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard proximal-map definition applied samplewise
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact samplewise proximal oracle; measurable selection and inexact variants are excluded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A sample proximal oracle queried with \((x,\lambda)\) draws \(\xi\) and returns a measurable selection \[P_\lambda(x,\xi)\in\arg\min_{y\in\mathbb{R}^d}\left\{f(y,\xi)+\frac{1}{2\lambda}\|y-x\|^2\right\}.\] Equivalently, \(P_\lambda(x,\xi)\in\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda f(\cdot,\xi)}(x)\). If the sample loss is \(\rho\)-weakly convex and \(0<\lambda<\rho^{-1}\), the proximal objective is strongly convex, so the returned point is unique. The oracle definition itself requires only existence of a measurable minimizing selection.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sample proximal oracle draws one sample and returns a minimizer of that sample loss plus a quadratic penalty around the query point.
knowledge_statements.title: Sample Proximal Oracles

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proximal formula is standard, but no citation supports its sample-oracle specialization. Existence of a minimizer almost surely does not alone guarantee the asserted measurable minimizing selection; suitable measurability and selection hypotheses are needed.

assumptions_latex: \(x\) and \(y\) belong to a finite-dimensional Euclidean space.
\(\xi\) is sampled from the oracle distribution.
For every query \(x\), the returned model is proper in its trial-point argument.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The oracle returns a random function \(m_x(\cdot,\xi)\) satisfying \(m_x(x,\xi)=f(x,\xi)\) almost surely.

notation.meaning: Random local model based at the query point.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: conventional exact-at-base stochastic local-model oracle
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Oracle representation only; model accuracy, weak convexity, and bias are separate conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A stochastic local-model oracle queried at \(x\) draws \(\xi\) and returns a proper random function \(m_x(\cdot,\xi)\) defined on the trial-point space. The model is anchored at the query point: \[m_x(x,\xi)=f(x,\xi)\quad\text{almost surely}.\] For each fixed \(x\) and \(y\), the quantity \(m_x(y,\xi)\) is measurable in \(\xi\). The model may be affine, proximal-linear, or otherwise structured. Any one-sided or two-sided comparison with the sample loss or population objective is an additional model-quality assumption, not part of this oracle representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A stochastic local-model oracle samples a random function anchored to the sampled loss at the current query point; accuracy and curvature require separate assumptions.
knowledge_statements.title: Stochastic Local-Model Oracles

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No inspectable source supports exact samplewise anchoring as the defining requirement for this stochastic local-model oracle family. This convention must be sourced because stochastic model frameworks use differing anchoring and accuracy assumptions.

assumptions_latex: \(F:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}\) is finite at the queried point.
The oracle noise is measurable and integrable whenever a mean condition is imposed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned observation has the representation \(Y(x,\xi)=F(x)+\varepsilon(x,\xi)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive scalar observation model; unbiasedness and tail behavior are optional regimes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A noisy function-value oracle queried at \(x\) returns a scalar \[Y(x,\xi)=F(x)+\varepsilon(x,\xi),\] where \(\xi\) contains the oracle randomness and \(\varepsilon(x,\xi)\) is the observation error. An unbiased value oracle additionally satisfies \(\mathbb{E}[\varepsilon(x,\xi)]=0\). A bounded-variance version satisfies \(\mathbb{E}[\varepsilon(x,\xi)^2]\leq\sigma^2\) for a stated \(\sigma<\infty\). Neither unbiasedness nor bounded variance follows from the noisy-oracle representation and must be declared separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A noisy value oracle returns the true objective value plus random scalar error; mean and variance restrictions are separate assumptions.
knowledge_statements.title: Noisy Function-Value Oracles

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The additive-noise representation and optional moment regimes are mathematically coherent, but the record supplies no citation for this exact noisy value-oracle convention.

assumptions_latex: \(x\in\mathbb{R}^d\) is fixed independently of the fresh oracle sample \(\xi\).
A designated generalized subdifferential \(\partial F(x)\) is fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There exists \(g(x)\in\partial F(x)\) such that \(\mathbb{E}[G(x,\xi)]=g(x)\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard pointwise unbiased stochastic-oracle condition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise unconditional unbiasedness for a specified generalized subdifferential.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A first-order oracle operates in the unbiased regime on a domain \(D\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\) when, for every fixed \(x\in D\), its output \(G(x,\xi)\) is integrable and there exists a selected generalized subgradient \(g(x)\in\partial F(x)\) satisfying \[\mathbb{E}[G(x,\xi)]=g(x).\] The expectation is taken over a fresh oracle sample at the fixed query. This condition does not by itself imply conditional unbiasedness when queries are random and history-dependent; that stronger adapted formulation must be imposed separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At every fixed query, the expected oracle output equals a selected generalized subgradient of the population objective.
knowledge_statements.title: Unbiased Oracle Regime

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition is plausible, but no source supports it and the designated generalized subdifferential is not identified. In nonconvex nonsmooth optimization, the choice of subdifferential materially affects the claim.

assumptions_latex: The oracle output \(G_k\) is integrable and observed after the query.
The generalized subdifferential \(\partial F\) is specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There is an \(\mathcal{F}_k\)-measurable \(g_k\in\partial F(x_k)\) with \(\mathbb{E}[G_k\mid\mathcal{F}_k]=g_k\) almost surely.

notation.meaning: Information available before the iteration-k oracle call.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: History-conditioned unbiasedness for adapted stochastic iterates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((\mathcal{F}_k)_{k\geq0}\) describe the information available immediately before the iteration-\(k\) oracle call, and let \(x_k\) be \(\mathcal{F}_k\)-measurable. The oracle is conditionally unbiased and adapted if its integrable output \(G_k\) admits an \(\mathcal{F}_k\)-measurable selection \(g_k\in\partial F(x_k)\) such that \[\mathbb{E}[G_k\mid\mathcal{F}_k]=g_k\quad\text{almost surely}.\] Equivalently, \(G_k-g_k\) is a martingale difference relative to the pre-oracle history and the enlarged filtration containing \(G_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Given all pre-query history, the expected oracle output equals a measurable generalized subgradient at the adapted current iterate.
knowledge_statements.title: Conditionally Unbiased Adapted Regime

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No citation supports this adapted nonsmooth-oracle condition. The martingale-difference equivalence also refers to an enlarged filtration without defining it or explicitly requiring G_k-g_k to be measurable with respect to the next information sigma-field.

assumptions_latex: \(x_k\) is measurable with respect to the pre-oracle filtration \(\mathcal{F}_k\).
The oracle output \(G_k\) is conditionally integrable.
A nonnegative \(\mathcal{F}_k\)-measurable bias allowance \(b_k\) is specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For some \(g_k\in\partial F(x_k)\), \(\|\mathbb{E}[G_k\mid\mathcal{F}_k]-g_k\|\leq b_k\) almost surely.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Norm-bounded conditional bias relative to a selected generalized subgradient.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An adapted oracle operates under controlled bias if, for every iteration \(k\), there exists an \(\mathcal{F}_k\)-measurable selection \(g_k\in\partial F(x_k)\) and a nonnegative \(\mathcal{F}_k\)-measurable allowance \(b_k\) such that \[\left\|\mathbb{E}[G_k\mid\mathcal{F}_k]-g_k\right\|\leq b_k\quad\text{almost surely}.\] The sequence \((b_k)\) quantifies systematic conditional error. Convergence results may additionally require \(b_k\to0\), summability of weighted biases, or a fixed bias floor; none of those asymptotic restrictions is part of the regime definition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The conditional mean oracle output may differ from a selected generalized subgradient, but the difference is bounded by a declared adapted bias allowance.
knowledge_statements.title: Controlled-Bias Regime

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The norm-bounded conditional-bias condition is coherent, but no source establishes that this is the intended controlled-bias regime, including the norm, subdifferential, and measurability convention.

assumptions_latex: The random local model \(m_x(y,\xi)\) is integrable for relevant \(x,y\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M_x(x)=F(x)\) and \(M_x(y)\leq F(y)+(\tau/2)\|y-x\|^2\) for all relevant \(x,y\).

notation.meaning: Expected model based at the query point.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: conventional upper one-sided quadratic model-error convention
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses the upper one-sided expected-model convention; alternative orientations require separate records.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the expected model by \(M_x(y)=\mathbb{E}[m_x(y,\xi)]\). Under the upper one-sided quadratic accuracy convention, the model is exact at its base point and never exceeds the population objective by more than a quadratic error: \[M_x(x)=F(x),\qquad M_x(y)-F(y)\leq\frac{\tau}{2}\|y-x\|^2\] for all relevant base points \(x\) and trial points \(y\). This condition controls only model overestimation; it imposes no lower bound on \(M_x(y)-F(y)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The expected model is exact at its base point and may overestimate the population objective by at most a quadratic displacement term.
knowledge_statements.title: One-Sided Model Accuracy

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The direction and expected-model interpretation of one-sided accuracy are convention-dependent. The builder explicitly flags the inequality direction as unconfirmed, and no citation resolves it.

assumptions_latex: The random model \(m_x(y,\xi)\) is integrable for relevant \(x,y\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|M_x(y)-F(y)|\leq(\tau/2)\|y-x\|^2\) for all relevant \(x,y\).

notation.meaning: Expected model based at the query point.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard symmetric quadratic model-error condition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Expected-model two-sided quadratic accuracy, not a samplewise almost-sure bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(M_x(y)=\mathbb{E}[m_x(y,\xi)]\). The model has two-sided quadratic accuracy with constant \(\tau\geq0\) when \[\left|M_x(y)-F(y)\right|\leq\frac{\tau}{2}\|y-x\|^2\] for every relevant base point \(x\) and trial point \(y\). Setting \(y=x\) gives \(M_x(x)=F(x)\). Equivalently, both \(M_x(y)\leq F(y)+(\tau/2)\|y-x\|^2\) and \(M_x(y)\geq F(y)-(\tau/2)\|y-x\|^2\) hold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The expected model differs from the population objective in either direction by at most a quadratic function of displacement from its base point.
knowledge_statements.title: Two-Sided Model Accuracy

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed two-sided bound is internally consistent, but no source confirms that this leaf concerns expected-model accuracy rather than a samplewise almost-sure or conditional bound.

assumptions_latex: For every base point \(x\), \(m_x(\cdot,\xi)\) is proper and lower semicontinuous almost surely.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \(x\), the function \(y\mapsto m_x(y,\xi)+(\rho/2)\|y-x\|^2\) is convex on \(D\) almost surely.

notation.meaning: Random local model based at the query point.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform almost-sure weak convexity of each sample model in its trial-point argument.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The stochastic model family is uniformly \(\rho\)-weakly convex when, for every base point \(x\in D\), the function \[y\longmapsto m_x(y,\xi)+\frac{\rho}{2}\|y-x\|^2\] is convex on \(D\) for almost every \(\xi\), with the same finite constant \(\rho\geq0\) for all base points and samples. Consequently, adding a proximal term with parameter \(\lambda\) makes the model subproblem strongly convex whenever \(0<\lambda<\rho^{-1}\), using the convention \(\rho^{-1}=+\infty\) when \(\rho=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every sampled local model becomes convex after adding the same quadratic curvature correction in its trial-point argument.
knowledge_statements.title: Sample-Model Weak Convexity

children.title: Deterministic Solution Inexactness
children.top_down_role: Covers controlled approximation error in model subproblem solutions.

assumptions_latex: The model subproblem objective \(Q_k\) has finite infimum \(Q_k^*\) and at least one minimizer.
A deterministic tolerance \(\varepsilon_k\geq0\) is prescribed before solving.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned point \(y_k\) satisfies \(Q_k(y_k)-Q_k^*\leq\varepsilon_k\).

notation.meaning: Exact optimal value of the subproblem.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard deterministic objective-gap inexactness criterion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic objective-gap criterion for an otherwise possibly random model subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q_k\) denote the realized model subproblem objective and let \(Q_k^*=\inf_y Q_k(y)\). A returned point \(y_k\) has deterministic solution inexactness \(\varepsilon_k\geq0\) when \[Q_k(y_k)-Q_k^*\leq\varepsilon_k\] holds for every admitted realization of the model and solver inputs. The tolerance \(\varepsilon_k\) is fixed before the inner solve and is not random. This criterion measures objective suboptimality; distance-to-solution and residual-based criteria are distinct unless additional growth or error-bound assumptions relate them.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each realized subproblem is solved to an objective gap no larger than a tolerance fixed before the inner solve.
knowledge_statements.title: Deterministic Solution Inexactness

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The deterministic objective-gap criterion fits the leaf and is mathematically coherent, but no inspectable source supports its realized-subproblem quantification or deterministic-tolerance convention.

children.title: Random Solver Error
children.top_down_role: Covers stochastic error introduced by randomized inner solvers.

assumptions_latex: The realized subproblem objective \(Q_k\) has finite optimal value \(Q_k^*\).
The inner solver may use auxiliary randomness \(\zeta_k\).
The returned point and its objective gap are measurable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The solver error is the nonnegative random variable \(\Delta_k=Q_k(y_k)-Q_k^*\).

notation.meaning: Auxiliary randomness used by the inner solver.
Random point returned by the inner solver.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: randomization of the standard objective-gap inexactness measure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Random objective-gap error only; conditional expectation or tail bounds are separate controls.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose an inner algorithm uses auxiliary randomness \(\zeta_k\) and returns a measurable point \(y_k=y_k(\zeta_k)\) for the realized subproblem \(Q_k\). Its random solver error is the nonnegative random variable \[\Delta_k:=Q_k(y_k)-Q_k^*,\qquad Q_k^*:=\inf_y Q_k(y).\] Thus \(Q_k(y_k)\leq Q_k^*+\Delta_k\) holds identically. The definition permits \(\Delta_k\) to depend on both the sampled model and inner-solver randomness; conditional mean, moment, or tail bounds on \(\Delta_k\) are additional error-control assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A randomized inner solver's error is the random objective gap between its returned point and the realized subproblem optimum.
knowledge_statements.title: Random Solver Error

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No citation supports defining random solver error specifically by objective gap. Moreover, finite Q_k^* does not ensure Q_k(y_k) is finite, so Delta_k need not be a finite real-valued random variable without an additional domain or finiteness assumption.

children.title: Conditional Error Control
children.top_down_role: Covers error control relative to the algorithmic information history.

knowledge_statements.title: Conditional Error Control
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional mean-square control for a random approximate solution of a stochastic model subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal F_k\) contain all information available before the inner solve, let \(Q_k\) be the realized subproblem objective, and let \(Q_k^*=\inf_y Q_k(y)\). A random inner output \(Y_k\) satisfies conditional error control with tolerance \(\varepsilon_k\ge 0\) if \(Y_k\) is measurable after the inner randomness is revealed and
\[\mathbb E\!\left[Q_k(Y_k)-Q_k^*\mid\mathcal F_k\right]\le \varepsilon_k\quad\text{a.s.}\]
For distance-based control, the corresponding condition is \(\mathbb E[\operatorname{dist}^2(Y_k,S_k^*)\mid\mathcal F_k]\le\varepsilon_k^2\) almost surely, where \(S_k^*=\operatorname*{argmin}Q_k\) is assumed nonempty.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Given the outer history, the expected inner objective gap—or squared distance to the solution set—is bounded by a prescribed tolerance almost surely.
assumptions_latex: \(Q_k^*>-\infty\) and the displayed conditional expectation exists.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E[Q_k(Y_k)-Q_k^*\mid\mathcal F_k]\le\varepsilon_k\) almost surely.

notation.meaning: outer history before the kth inner solve

review_flags: objective-gap and distance variants should be source-certified

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind and terminal placement fit, but the objective-gap and distance-based formulations require a source establishing their precise conditional measurability and integrability conventions.

children.title: Inner-Solve Complexity Effects
children.top_down_role: Covers how solution accuracy changes total computational work.

knowledge_statements.title: Inner-Solve Complexity Effects
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Accounting identity and rate consequence for nested stochastic methods with tolerance-dependent inner work.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose an outer method performs \(T\) iterations and, at iteration \(k\), an inner solver needs at most \(K(\varepsilon_k)\) oracle calls to attain the stipulated conditional error tolerance \(\varepsilon_k\). Then the total inner-oracle cost is bounded by
\[N_{\mathrm{in}}\le \sum_{k=0}^{T-1}K(\varepsilon_k).\]
In particular, if \(K(\varepsilon)\le C\varepsilon^{-p}\) for constants \(C>0\), \(p>0\), and a uniform tolerance \(\varepsilon_k=\varepsilon\) is required, then \(N_{\mathrm{in}}\le CT\varepsilon^{-p}\). Thus an outer iteration bound alone does not represent the end-to-end oracle complexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Total inner work is the sum of tolerance-dependent solve costs; polynomial inner accuracy costs multiply the outer iteration count under a uniform tolerance.
assumptions_latex: Each inner solve reaches tolerance \(\varepsilon_k\) within \(K(\varepsilon_k)\) oracle calls.
The outer method executes exactly \(T\) inner solves.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N_{\mathrm{in}}\le\sum_{k=0}^{T-1}K(\varepsilon_k)\), and uniformly \(N_{\mathrm{in}}\le CT\varepsilon^{-p}\) when \(K(\varepsilon)\le C\varepsilon^{-p}\).

notation.meaning: inner oracle complexity at tolerance epsilon

review_flags: method-specific tolerance schedules require separate certification
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

knowledge_statements.title: Bounded Second-Moment Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform unconditional second-moment assumption for a stochastic first-order oracle.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^d\), let \(x\in X\), and let \(G(x,\xi)\) be a measurable stochastic oracle vector. The oracle operates in the bounded second-moment regime if there exists \(M<\infty\) such that
\[\sup_{x\in X}\mathbb E_{\xi}\!\left[\lVert G(x,\xi)\rVert^2\right]\le M^2.\]
This condition bounds both the squared norm of the mean oracle, whenever it exists, and its variance through \(\lVert\mathbb E G(x,\xi)\rVert^2\le\mathbb E\lVert G(x,\xi)\rVert^2\). It does not impose exponential tails or an almost-sure bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The oracle vector has a uniformly bounded second moment over the feasible domain, without requiring bounded samples or exponential tails.
assumptions_latex: The expectation is taken with respect to the oracle sampling law.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sup_{x\in X}\mathbb E\lVert G(x,\xi)\rVert^2\le M^2\).

source_refs.locator: 4.2 The Gradient Method in the Presence of Noise p. 98

review_flags: locator may discuss a narrower noisy-gradient setting

source_witnesses.locator: 4.2 The Gradient Method in the Presence of Noise p. 98

knowledge_statements.title: Bounded Conditional-Variance Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Martingale-difference oracle noise with variance uniformly bounded conditionally on the algorithmic history.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \((\mathcal F_k)_{k\ge0}\) be the algorithmic filtration, let \(x_k\) be \(\mathcal F_k\)-measurable, and write \(G_k=g_k+\zeta_k\), where \(g_k=\mathbb E[G_k\mid\mathcal F_k]\). The bounded conditional-variance regime holds if there is \(\sigma<\infty\) such that, for every \(k\),
\[\mathbb E[\zeta_k\mid\mathcal F_k]=0,
\qquad \mathbb E[\lVert\zeta_k\rVert^2\mid\mathcal F_k]\le\sigma^2
\quad\text{a.s.}\]
Unlike a bounded second moment for \(G_k\), this permits the predictable component \(g_k\) to be unbounded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After conditioning on the current history, oracle noise is mean zero and has uniformly bounded variance, while the predictable oracle component may remain unbounded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E[\zeta_k\mid\mathcal F_k]=0\) and \(\mathbb E[\lVert\zeta_k\rVert^2\mid\mathcal F_k]\le\sigma^2\) almost surely.

notation.meaning: history before the kth oracle sample

review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

children.title: Relative Noise Regimes
children.top_down_role: Covers stochastic error scaled to an objective or stationarity quantity.

knowledge_statements.title: Relative Noise Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional noise variance controlled relative to a predictable stationarity or oracle scale.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G_k=g_k+\zeta_k\), with \(g_k=\mathbb E[G_k\mid\mathcal F_k]\). A relative-noise regime with parameters \(\sigma_0,\sigma_1\ge0\) holds when
\[\mathbb E[\zeta_k\mid\mathcal F_k]=0,
\qquad
\mathbb E[\lVert\zeta_k\rVert^2\mid\mathcal F_k]
\le \sigma_0^2+\sigma_1^2\lVert g_k\rVert^2
\quad\text{a.s.}\]
The purely relative case has \(\sigma_0=0\); then the admissible variance vanishes whenever \(g_k=0\). The additive-plus-relative case permits a nonzero noise floor \(\sigma_0^2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Conditional variance is bounded by an additive floor plus a term proportional to the squared predictable oracle magnitude.
assumptions_latex: \(g_k\) is an appropriate predictable oracle or stationarity vector.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E[\lVert\zeta_k\rVert^2\mid\mathcal F_k]\le\sigma_0^2+\sigma_1^2\lVert g_k\rVert^2\) almost surely.
review_flags: source concerns deterministic relative noise and only indirectly supports the stochastic conditional formulation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cited locator concerns deterministic relative noise and does not directly support the conditional stochastic variance model or its additive-plus-relative interpretation.

children.title: State-Dependent Noise Growth
children.top_down_role: Covers noise magnitude that varies with iterate location.

knowledge_statements.title: State-Dependent Noise Growth
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional variance allowed to grow with a measurable state-dependent scale.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\) be a state space, let \(x_k\in X\) be \(\mathcal F_k\)-measurable, and let \(G_k=g(x_k)+\zeta_k\), where \(\mathbb E[\zeta_k\mid\mathcal F_k]=0\). Given a measurable growth function \(V:X\to[0,\infty)\), the oracle has state-dependent noise growth if constants \(a,b\ge0\) satisfy
\[\mathbb E[\lVert\zeta_k\rVert^2\mid\mathcal F_k]\le a+bV(x_k)\quad\text{a.s. for every }k.\]
Common choices include \(V(x)=\lVert x\rVert^2\), an objective gap, or a squared stationarity measure; the chosen scale must be specified in any convergence result.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Oracle variance may grow with the current iterate through an explicitly chosen nonnegative state scale, rather than obeying a uniform bound.
assumptions_latex: The centered noise \(\zeta_k\) is conditionally square-integrable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E[\lVert\zeta_k\rVert^2\mid\mathcal F_k]\le a+bV(x_k)\) almost surely.

notation.meaning: state space containing every iterate x_k

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: affine state-dependent conditional variance model
specific admissible growth scales are theorem-dependent
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

children.title: Near-Stationary Noise Behavior
children.top_down_role: Covers noise scaling near stationary regions.

knowledge_statements.title: Near-Stationary Noise Behavior
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limiting noise floor implied by variance growth tied continuously to a stationarity measure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(s:X\to[0,\infty)\) be a stationarity measure and suppose
\[\mathbb E[\lVert\zeta_k\rVert^2\mid\mathcal F_k]
\le \sigma_0^2+\sigma_1^2s(x_k)^2\quad\text{a.s.}\]
If \(s(x_k)\to0\) almost surely, then
\[\limsup_{k\to\infty}\mathbb E[\lVert\zeta_k\rVert^2\mid\mathcal F_k]
\le\sigma_0^2\quad\text{a.s.}\]
Consequently, purely relative noise with \(\sigma_0=0\) vanishes in conditional mean square near stationarity, whereas \(\sigma_0>0\) leaves a persistent variance floor.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: As the stationarity measure vanishes, relative noise disappears, but additive noise converges only to its residual variance floor.
assumptions_latex: The displayed conditional variance bound holds for every \(k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\limsup_{k\to\infty}\mathbb E[\lVert\zeta_k\rVert^2\mid\mathcal F_k]\le\sigma_0^2\) almost surely.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: direct limiting consequence of the stated variance inequality
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

children.title: Noise-Growth Instability
children.top_down_role: Covers regimes where stochastic growth overwhelms geometric control.

knowledge_statements.title: Noise-Growth Instability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure mechanism when state-dependent variance outgrows the algorithm's stabilizing drift.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider the scalar recursion \(x_{k+1}=x_k-\alpha(x_k+\zeta_k)\), where \(0<\alpha<2\), \(c\ge0\), \(\mathbb E[\zeta_k\mid\mathcal F_k]=0\), and
\[\mathbb E[\zeta_k^2\mid\mathcal F_k]=c x_k^2.\]
Then
\[\mathbb E[x_{k+1}^2\mid\mathcal F_k]=\bigl((1-\alpha)^2+\alpha^2c\bigr)x_k^2.\]
Hence mean-square contraction fails whenever \((1-\alpha)^2+\alpha^2c\ge1\), equivalently \(c\ge 2/\alpha-1\). Thus even multiplicative, conditionally unbiased noise can destabilize an otherwise contracting iteration when its growth coefficient is too large.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Multiplicative unbiased noise destroys mean-square contraction once its nonnegative growth coefficient overwhelms deterministic drift; the scalar threshold is explicit.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Mean-square contraction fails for \(c\ge2/\alpha-1\).

notation.meaning: history before the kth noise realization

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: exact conditional second-moment calculation for the displayed recursion
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

knowledge_statements.title: Light-Tailed Noise Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional sub-Gaussian control of every directional projection of centered oracle noise.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\zeta_k=G_k-\mathbb E[G_k\mid\mathcal F_k]\in\mathbb R^d\). The oracle noise is conditionally \(\sigma\)-sub-Gaussian if, for every \(u\in\mathbb R^d\) and \(\lambda\in\mathbb R\),
\[\mathbb E\!\left[\exp\!\left(\lambda\langle u,\zeta_k\rangle\right)\mid\mathcal F_k\right]\le \exp\!\left(\frac{\lambda^2\sigma^2\lVert u\rVert^2}{2}\right)\quad\text{a.s.}\]
This implies conditional mean zero and, for every \(u\ne0\) and \(t\ge0\), Gaussian-type projection tails:
\[\mathbb P\!\left(\lvert\langle u,\zeta_k\rangle\rvert\ge t\mid\mathcal F_k\right)\le2\exp\!\left(-\frac{t^2}{2\sigma^2\lVert u\rVert^2}\right)\quad\text{a.s.}\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every directional projection of centered oracle noise has a conditional moment-generating function bounded by that of a Gaussian; every nonzero projection consequently has the corresponding Gaussian-type tail bound.
assumptions_latex: The moment-generating function exists for all displayed \(u\) and \(\lambda\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E[\exp(\lambda\langle u,\zeta_k\rangle)\mid\mathcal F_k]\le\exp(\lambda^2\sigma^2\lVert u\rVert^2/2)\) almost surely.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard conditional sub-Gaussian vector definition
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

children.title: Heavy-Tailed Oracle Noise
children.top_down_role: Covers oracle distributions beyond classical light-tail assumptions.

knowledge_statements.title: Heavy-Tailed Oracle Noise
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-moment oracle regime without an assumed exponential moment-generating function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G(x,\xi)=g(x)+\zeta(x,\xi)\), where \(\mathbb E[\zeta(x,\xi)\mid x]=0\). For a fixed \(p\in(1,2]\), a finite-\(p\)-moment heavy-tail regime assumes a constant \(M_p<\infty\) satisfying
\[\sup_{x\in X}\mathbb E[\lVert\zeta(x,\xi)\rVert^p\mid x]\le M_p^p.\]
No exponential-moment or almost-sure bound is imposed. When \(p<2\), the second moment may be infinite, so sample-mean guarantees based on conditional variance need not apply; robust aggregation or clipping is then required for high-confidence control.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Centered oracle noise has only a finite moment of order between one and two; variance or exponential moments may not exist.
assumptions_latex: The conditional mean \(\mathbb E[\zeta(x,\xi)\mid x]\) exists and equals zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sup_{x\in X}\mathbb E[\lVert\zeta(x,\xi)\rVert^p\mid x]\le M_p^p\), without a sub-Gaussian tail assumption.

notation.meaning: centered oracle noise at state x

review_flags: heavy-tail convention varies across stochastic-optimization literature
finite-p-moment formulation requires an authoritative locator

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite-p-moment condition fits the leaf, but heavy-tail conventions vary, and the assertion that robust aggregation or clipping is required for high-confidence control is method- and guarantee-dependent and needs authoritative support.

children.title: Robust Gradient Estimation
children.top_down_role: Covers robust estimators used for stochastic first-order information.

knowledge_statements.title: Robust Gradient Estimation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Geometric median-of-means estimator for a mean oracle vector under finite variance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given independent oracle vectors \(G_1,\ldots,G_n\in\mathbb R^d\), choose \(B\le n\) nonempty blocks \(I_1,\ldots,I_B\), compute block means \(\bar G_b=|I_b|^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_b}G_i\), and output
\[\widehat g\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{z\in\mathbb R^d}
\sum_{b=1}^{B}\lVert z-\bar G_b\rVert.\]
The output is a geometric median of the block means. With \(B\) proportional to \(\log(1/\delta)\), this aggregation converts constant-probability concentration of each block mean into a confidence level \(1-\delta\), provided strictly more than half of the block means lie in a common accuracy ball.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Partition oracle samples, average within blocks, and return a geometric median of block means to obtain high-confidence resistance to heavy-tailed samples.
assumptions_latex: \(G_1,\ldots,G_n\) are independent with a common finite mean.
A strict majority of block means satisfy the required constant-probability accuracy event.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat g\) is the geometric median-of-means aggregate of the sampled oracle vectors.

notation.meaning: mean oracle vector in block b

review_flags: geometric median-of-means guarantee needs a precise theorem and constants
independence and block-size requirements require source certification

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind and geometric median-of-means construction fit the terminal container, but the confidence claim requires a precise theorem specifying independent blocks, per-block success probability, block sizes, and constants.

children.title: Robust Model Estimation
children.top_down_role: Covers robust aggregation of stochastic local models.

knowledge_statements.title: Robust Model Estimation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise median-of-means aggregation of stochastic model values under finite variance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix a model query pair \((x,y)\) and draw independent stochastic model values \(M_1(y;x),\ldots,M_n(y;x)\) with common mean \(m(y;x)\). Partition the indices into \(B\) nonempty blocks \(I_b\), form
\[\bar M_b(y;x)=\frac{1}{|I_b|}\sum_{i\in I_b}M_i(y;x),\]
and output
\[\widehat m(y;x)=\operatorname{median}\{\bar M_1(y;x),\ldots,\bar M_B(y;x)\}.\]
For simultaneous estimation over multiple query pairs, the same blocks may be reused, but any uniform error guarantee must account explicitly for the size or complexity of the query class.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Average stochastic model values within blocks and take their median; uniform model guarantees additionally depend on the complexity of the queried model class.
assumptions_latex: For fixed \((x,y)\), the sampled model values are independent with common finite mean and variance.
The number and sizes of blocks are fixed before inspecting their values.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat m(y;x)=\operatorname{median}_{1\le b\le B}\bar M_b(y;x)\) is the pointwise robust model estimate.

notation.meaning: ith stochastic model value at query pair (x,y)

review_flags: pointwise statement does not itself provide a uniform model-quality guarantee

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind and pointwise median-of-means construction fit the leaf, but no source supports its use for stochastic model estimation or the stated interface with uniform query-class guarantees.

children.title: Contamination Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Covers robustness limits under corrupted or adversarial samples.

knowledge_statements.title: Contamination Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identifiability boundary for Huber-contaminated stochastic-oracle observations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the observed oracle law be \(Q=(1-\varepsilon)P+\varepsilon R\), where \(0\leq\varepsilon<1\), \(P\) is the clean law, and \(R\) is arbitrary. If two clean laws satisfy \(\operatorname{TV}(P_0,P_1)\leq \varepsilon/(1-\varepsilon)\), their contamination neighborhoods intersect: there exist \(R_0,R_1\) with \((1-\varepsilon)P_0+\varepsilon R_0=(1-\varepsilon)P_1+\varepsilon R_1\). Consequently, for any estimator \(\widehat\theta\) and any metric \(d\), if \(d(\theta(P_0),\theta(P_1))=\Delta\), then under the common observed law, \(\max_{j\in\{0,1\}}\mathbb E[d(\widehat\theta,\theta(P_j))]\geq \Delta/2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Clean oracle laws closer than the contamination threshold can generate identical observations, forcing estimation error at least half their parameter separation.
assumptions_latex: \(d\) is a metric and the displayed risks are finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{TV}(P_0,P_1)\leq\varepsilon/(1-\varepsilon)\) permits observational equivalence and implies minimax error at least \(\Delta/2\).

notation.meaning: Target parameter of the clean oracle law.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role fits the container and the claim is mathematically plausible, but the exact Huber-neighborhood intersection threshold and resulting lower bound lack inspectable authoritative support.

knowledge_statements.title: Independent Sampling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional independence formulation for adaptive stochastic-oracle calls.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal F_t\) contain all iterates, oracle outputs, and algorithmic randomness available before sample \(\xi_t\) is drawn. Independent sampling from a fixed law \(P\) means that, for every measurable set \(A\), \(\mathbb P(\xi_t\in A\mid\mathcal F_t)=P(A)\) almost surely. Thus the samples are independent of the adaptive query history and identically distributed according to \(P\). For any integrable oracle map \(G\), this gives \(\mathbb E[G(x_t,\xi_t)\mid\mathcal F_t]=\mathbb E_{\xi\sim P}[G(x_t,\xi)]\) whenever \(x_t\) is \(\mathcal F_t\)-measurable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each fresh sample has the same fixed distribution and is independent of the complete adaptive history preceding its draw.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E[G(x_t,\xi_t)\mid\mathcal F_t]=\mathbb E_{\xi\sim P}[G(x_t,\xi)]\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The conditional-i.i.d. formulation is precise and fits Independent Sampling, but no inspectable stochastic-approximation or probability source is supplied.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Sum Index Sampling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Index-oracle model for a finite-sum weakly convex objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n f_i(x)\). At iteration \(t\), draw an index \(I_t\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\) with conditional probabilities \(p_{t,i}=\mathbb P(I_t=i\mid\mathcal F_t)>0\), and query a component subgradient \(g_{I_t}(x_t)\in\partial f_{I_t}(x_t)\). The importance-weighted oracle \(G_t=g_{I_t}(x_t)/(n p_{t,I_t})\) satisfies \(\mathbb E[G_t\mid\mathcal F_t]=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n g_i(x_t)\). Under uniform sampling, \(p_{t,i}=1/n\) and no weighting is needed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A component index selects one finite-sum term; inverse-probability weighting makes the sampled subgradient unbiased for the averaged selection.
assumptions_latex: \(f=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n f_i\) and each selected component admits a subgradient.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E[G_t\mid\mathcal F_t]=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n g_i(x_t)\).

notation.meaning: Conditional probability of selecting component i.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits finite-sum index sampling, but the identity requires measurable, integrable, history-measurable selections g_i(x_t) for every component, not merely the queried subgradient. A source is needed to settle the intended oracle formulation.

knowledge_statements.title: Minibatch Sampling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditionally independent minibatching and its variance reduction identity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given the pre-sampling history \(\mathcal F_t\), draw \(b\) conditionally independent samples \(\xi_{t,1},\ldots,\xi_{t,b}\) from a fixed law \(P\), and form \(\bar G_t=b^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^b G(x_t,\xi_{t,j})\). If \(g(x_t)=\mathbb E_{\xi\sim P}[G(x_t,\xi)]\) and \(\mathbb E[\lVert G(x_t,\xi)-g(x_t)\rVert^2\mid\mathcal F_t]\leq\sigma^2\), then \(\mathbb E[\bar G_t\mid\mathcal F_t]=g(x_t)\) and \(\mathbb E[\lVert\bar G_t-g(x_t)\rVert^2\mid\mathcal F_t]\leq\sigma^2/b\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Averaging b conditionally independent unbiased oracle calls preserves the mean and divides the conditional variance bound by b.
assumptions_latex: The batch samples are conditionally independent with common law \(P\).
The oracle has conditional second central moment at most \(\sigma^2\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E[\bar G_t\mid\mathcal F_t]=g(x_t)\) and \(\mathbb E[\lVert\bar G_t-g(x_t)\rVert^2\mid\mathcal F_t]\leq\sigma^2/b\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: variance of an independent sample mean

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The minibatch role is appropriate, but the stated squared-norm variance reduction requires a Euclidean or Hilbert-space norm and conditional unbiasedness. Those hypotheses and authoritative support are missing.

knowledge_statements.title: Without-Replacement Sampling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Random-permutation sampling within finite-sum epochs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an epoch, draw a permutation \(\pi\) uniformly from all permutations of \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\), then query components in the order \(I_k=\pi(k)\), \(k=1,\ldots,n\). Conditional on the previously revealed indices \(I_1,\ldots,I_{k-1}\), the next index is uniform on the remaining set: \(\mathbb P(I_k=i\mid I_1,\ldots,I_{k-1})=1/(n-k+1)\) for every unvisited \(i\). Hence the indices within an epoch are dependent, although every position has uniform marginal distribution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A random permutation visits every finite-sum component exactly once per epoch; positions are marginally uniform but mutually dependent.
assumptions_latex: The epoch permutation is uniform and drawn independently of the pre-epoch history.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{I_1,\ldots,I_n\}=\{1,\ldots,n\}\) almost surely, with conditional uniformity over unvisited indices.

notation.meaning: Component selected at position k of the epoch.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The random-permutation condition is internally consistent and fits the container, but no inspectable random-reshuffling source is supplied.

children.title: Markovian Sampling
children.top_down_role: Covers samples generated by a Markov process.

knowledge_statements.title: Markovian Sampling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Time-homogeneous Markov data with stationary target law.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A sampling process \((\xi_t)_{t\geq0}\) is Markovian with transition kernel \(K\) if, for every measurable set \(A\), \(\mathbb P(\xi_{t+1}\in A\mid\xi_0,\ldots,\xi_t)=K(\xi_t,A)\) almost surely. A probability law \(\pi\) is stationary when \(\pi K=\pi\). For stochastic-oracle analysis relative to \(\pi\), a quantitative mixing condition additionally requires a sequence \(r_t\downarrow0\) such that \(\sup_z\lVert K^t(z,\cdot)-\pi\rVert_{\operatorname{TV}}\leq r_t\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Samples follow a Markov transition kernel whose iterates approach a stationary target distribution at a specified total-variation rate.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a Markov transition kernel on a measurable state space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sup_z\lVert K^t(z,\cdot)-\pi\rVert_{\operatorname{TV}}\leq r_t\to0\) supplies the dependence-control rate.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record blends the general Markov property with the substantially stronger uniform total-variation ergodicity condition. A source is needed to establish which Markovian sampling regime belongs in this terminal container.

children.title: Mixing-Sequence Sampling
children.top_down_role: Covers temporally dependent samples controlled by mixing behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Mixing-Sequence Sampling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strong-mixing control for a stationary dependent oracle sequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a stationary sequence \((\xi_t)_{t\in\mathbb Z}\), define \(\mathcal F_a^b=\sigma(\xi_s:a\leq s\leq b)\) and the strong-mixing coefficient \(\alpha(k)=\sup_{A\in\mathcal F_{-\infty}^0,\,B\in\mathcal F_k^\infty}\lvert\mathbb P(A\cap B)-\mathbb P(A)\mathbb P(B)\rvert\). The process is strongly mixing when \(\alpha(k)\to0\). A summable mixing regime of order \(q>0\) requires \(\sum_{k=1}^\infty\alpha(k)^q<\infty\), providing quantitative decay sufficient for many dependent-sample moment bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dependence between the distant past and future vanishes, with summability imposing a quantitative rate usable in stochastic error bounds.
assumptions_latex: All sigma-fields are taken on a common probability space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\alpha(k)\to0\), with the stronger regime \(\sum_{k\geq1}\alpha(k)^q<\infty\).

notation.meaning: Sigma-field generated by samples indexed from a through b.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The strong-mixing definition fits the container, but the assertion that an arbitrary power-summability condition suffices for dependent-sample moment bounds depends on additional moment assumptions and the particular bound. No authoritative source is supplied.

children.title: Distribution-Drift Sampling
children.top_down_role: Covers time-varying sample distributions.

knowledge_statements.title: Distribution-Drift Sampling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonstationary sampling controlled by successive or target-law drift.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P_t=\mathcal L(\xi_t\mid\mathcal F_t)\) be the conditional sampling law and let \(P_\star\) be a reference law. Distribution drift is controlled by nonnegative sequences \((\delta_t)\) and \((\Delta_t)\) when \(\operatorname{TV}(P_{t+1},P_t)\leq\delta_t\) and \(\operatorname{TV}(P_t,P_\star)\leq\Delta_t\) almost surely. For every bounded measurable \(h\), this implies \(\lvert\mathbb E_{P_t}h-\mathbb E_{P_\star}h\rvert\leq2\lVert h\rVert_\infty\Delta_t\), under the convention \(\operatorname{TV}(P,Q)=\sup_A\lvert P(A)-Q(A)\rvert\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Time-varying sample laws remain close to consecutive or reference laws, which directly bounds bias for every bounded oracle statistic.
assumptions_latex: \(P_t\) and \(P_\star\) are probability laws on one measurable space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lvert\mathbb E_{P_t}h-\mathbb E_{P_\star}h\rvert\leq2\lVert h\rVert_\infty\Delta_t\).

notation.meaning: Conditional sampling law at time t.
Total-variation distance bound to the reference law.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The total-variation bias inequality is standard under the stated convention, but pathwise comparison of the random conditional laws P_t and P_{t+1} requires specified regular conditional distributions and measurability. The intended drift regime lacks a source.

children.title: Uncontrolled Dependence Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Covers dependence patterns outside available stochastic guarantees.

knowledge_statements.title: Uncontrolled Dependence Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Perfect dependence defeats averaging despite correct one-sample marginals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Z\) be a nondegenerate, mean-zero random vector with \(\mathbb E\lVert Z\rVert^2<\infty\), and set \(\xi_t=Z\) for every \(t\). Each sample has the same centered marginal law, but \(\bar\xi_T=T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^T\xi_t=Z\) almost surely. Therefore \(\mathbb E\lVert\bar\xi_T\rVert^2=\mathbb E\lVert Z\rVert^2\) for every \(T\), rather than decreasing as \(T^{-1}\). Marginal unbiasedness and finite variance alone consequently cannot justify stochastic-oracle averaging rates without independence, mixing, martingale-difference structure, or another dependence restriction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Perfectly dependent centered samples never average out, so unbiased marginals and finite variance alone cannot yield variance reduction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E\lVert T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^T\xi_t\rVert^2=\mathbb E\lVert Z\rVert^2\) for all \(T\).

notation.meaning: Single random vector reused at every time.
Average of the first T samples.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The explicit perfect-dependence counterexample is correct and its content kind fits the boundary container, but the record supplies only a standard-field rationale and no inspectable source for the broader dependence-boundary claim.
