knowledge_statements.title: Inexact Subproblem Solves
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Converts a strongly convex subproblem objective gap into distance accuracy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q:\mathbb{R}^d\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, closed, and \(\mu\)-strongly convex with minimizer \(z^\star\). A computed point \(\widehat z\) is a \(\delta\)-objective-accurate inexact solve when \(Q(\widehat z)-Q(z^\star)\leq\delta\). Strong convexity gives \(Q(\widehat z)-Q(z^\star)\geq(\mu/2)\|\widehat z-z^\star\|^2\); therefore the objective-gap certificate guarantees \(\|\widehat z-z^\star\|\leq\sqrt{2\delta/\mu}\). When a computable lower bound \(L_Q\leq Q(z^\star)\) is available, the verifiable inequality \(Q(\widehat z)-L_Q\leq\delta\) suffices.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A certified objective gap for a strongly convex subproblem bounds the distance between the computed and exact solutions.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\) is proper, closed, and \(\mu\)-strongly convex with \(\mu>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q(\widehat z)-Q(z^\star)\leq\delta\Longrightarrow\|\widehat z-z^\star\|\leq\sqrt{2\delta/\mu}\).

notation.meaning: computable lower bound on the optimum

children.title: Inner Accuracy Budgets

knowledge_statements.title: Inner Accuracy Budgets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: States a sufficient cumulative-error budget for an inexact outer descent recursion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose nonnegative sequences satisfy \(V_{k+1}\leq V_k-a_kS_k+b_k\delta_k\), where \(a_k>0\), \(b_k\geq0\), and \(\delta_k\geq0\) is the inner-solve error. An admissible inner accuracy budget is any sequence obeying \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}b_k\delta_k<\infty\). Summing the recursion then yields \(\sum_{k=0}^{T-1}a_kS_k\leq V_0-V_T+\sum_{k=0}^{T-1}b_k\delta_k\). If \(V_T\geq0\), the cumulative stationarity or descent measure remains bounded; if additionally \(\sum_ka_k=\infty\), then \(\liminf_k S_k=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose inner tolerances so their weighted cumulative error is finite; then inexactness does not overwhelm outer descent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_kb_k\delta_k<\infty\ \text{and}\ \sum_ka_k=\infty\Longrightarrow\liminf_{k\to\infty}S_k=0\).

children.title: Inner–Outer Work Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Covers the balance between subproblem effort and outer progress.

knowledge_statements.title: Inner–Outer Work Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Expresses total nested work as an accuracy-allocation problem and gives its interior optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Run \(T\in\mathbb N\) outer iterations and assign inner objective tolerances \(\delta_0,\ldots,\delta_{T-1}\) with \(0<\delta_k\leq D_k\). Suppose the outer analysis permits \(\sum_{k=0}^{T-1}b_k\delta_k\leq B\), while the modeled inner cost is \(C_k(\delta_k)=c_k\log(D_k/\delta_k)\). The least modeled inner work is \(\min\{\sum_{k=0}^{T-1}c_k\log(D_k/\delta_k):\sum_{k=0}^{T-1}b_k\delta_k\leq B,\ 0<\delta_k\leq D_k\}\). If \(0<B<\sum_{k=0}^{T-1}b_kD_k\) and \(c_kB/(b_k\sum_{j=0}^{T-1}c_j)<D_k\) for every \(k\), the unique optimum is interior and satisfies \(\delta_k^\star=c_kB/(b_k\sum_{j=0}^{T-1}c_j)\). If an upper bound is active, the optimum instead requires the corresponding bound-constrained reallocation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nested work can be represented as an accuracy-allocation problem. When no tolerance upper bound is active, larger errors are allocated to expensive solves and smaller errors where the outer method is more sensitive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\delta_k^\star=\frac{c_kB}{b_k\sum_{j=0}^{T-1}c_j}\quad(k=0,\ldots,T-1)\).

notation.meaning: modeled inner work at outer iteration k

Consequently, for any fixed \(x\),
\[
\mathbb E\bigl[g_{\pi(j+1)}(x)\mid\mathcal F_j\bigr]
=\frac1{|R_j|}\sum_{i\in R_j}g_i(x),
\]
which generally differs from \(n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^{n}g_i(x)\). Therefore the usual conditional-unbiasedness identity for fresh independent sampling cannot be assumed inside a reshuffled epoch.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Without-replacement sampling is uniform only over unvisited indices, so the next oracle value depends on prior selections and is generally not conditionally unbiased.
knowledge_statements.title: Reuse-Induced Dependence

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property content kind fits Reuse-Induced Dependence. The conditional law and remaining-set average are mathematically coherent, but the record has no inspectable citation supporting its use as a reshuffling dependence statement in this chapter.

children.title: Data-Retention Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Covers memory and access costs associated with retained samples.

assumptions_latex: A dataset contains \(n\) records, each requiring \(s\) storage units.
A streaming alternative retains only a working state of size \(m\).
Reusing a stored record incurs one indexed access and no new data acquisition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Full reuse requires \(ns+O(m)\) storage, while streaming requires \(O(m)\); each reuse replaces one acquisition by one retained-data access.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: direct storage and access accounting for retained finite data
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract memory-access accounting; statistical and hardware-dependent effects are excluded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Retaining all \(n\) records requires
\[
M_{\mathrm{reuse}}=ns+O(m)
\]
storage units, whereas a one-pass streaming interface with no retained records requires \(M_{\mathrm{stream}}=O(m)\). If \(K\) post-acquisition oracle evaluations revisit stored records, reuse incurs \(K\) retained-data accesses and zero additional acquisitions; a fresh-sample interface instead incurs \(K\) acquisitions. This accounting states a resource tradeoff only and does not order the two interfaces statistically or computationally without a cost model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Retaining all data costs ns storage but permits later oracle calls through indexed access instead of new acquisition; streaming uses only working-state memory.
knowledge_statements.title: Data-Retention Tradeoffs

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity_bound content kind fits Data-Retention Tradeoffs, and the statement clearly limits itself to an abstract storage-and-access model. The asserted model and accounting have no cited source or inspectable locator.

assumptions_latex: For almost every sample \(\xi\), the function \(x\mapsto f(x,\xi)\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and \(\rho(\xi)\)-weakly convex.
The measurable modulus satisfies \(0\leq\rho(\xi)\leq\bar\rho<\infty\) almost surely.
The expectation \(F(x)=\mathbb E[f(x,\xi)]\) is well-defined and proper.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The population objective \(F\) is \(\bar\rho\)-weakly convex, so any valid essential upper bound on sample moduli is a conservative calibration.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional expectation model with an almost-sure uniform modulus bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Samplewise weak convexity means that, almost surely,
\[
x\longmapsto f(x,\xi)+\frac{\rho(\xi)}2\|x\|^2
\]
is convex. If \(\rho(\xi)\leq\bar\rho\) almost surely, then
\[
x\longmapsto F(x)+\frac{\bar\rho}{2}\|x\|^2
=\mathbb E\left[f(x,\xi)+\frac{\bar\rho}{2}\|x\|^2\right]
\]
is convex. Hence \(\bar\rho\) is a valid weak-convexity parameter for \(F\); choosing a smaller value requires separate justification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An almost-sure upper bound on samplewise weak-convexity moduli is a valid conservative modulus for the expected objective.
knowledge_statements.title: Weak-Convexity Parameter Calibration

children.title: Regularization Calibration
children.top_down_role: Covers selection of proximal or model regularization strength.

assumptions_latex: The function \(F:\mathbb R^d\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and \(\rho\)-weakly convex.
The proximal regularization parameter satisfies \(0<\lambda<1/\rho\), with \(1/0=+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The proximal subproblem has a unique minimizer for every center, and the Moreau envelope is continuously differentiable.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Moreau regularization calibrated strictly below the reciprocal weak-convexity modulus.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For each \(x\in\mathbb R^d\), define
\[
F_\lambda(x)=\min_y\left\{F(y)+\frac{1}{2\lambda}\|y-x\|^2\right\}.
\]
The calibration condition is \(0<\lambda<1/\rho\). Under it, the minimized objective is \((1/\lambda-\rho)\)-strongly convex, so \(\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda F}(x)\) is single-valued, and
\[
\nabla F_\lambda(x)=\lambda^{-1}\bigl(x-\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda F}(x)\bigr).
\]
At \(\lambda=1/\rho\), strong convexity and uniqueness are not guaranteed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose the Moreau parameter strictly below the reciprocal weak-convexity modulus; this makes each proximal subproblem strongly convex and its minimizer unique.
knowledge_statements.title: Regularization Calibration

children.title: Stepsize Calibration
children.top_down_role: Covers selection of stochastic update scales.

assumptions_latex: Iterates satisfy a descent estimate with expected error term \(C\alpha_t^2\), where \(C<infty\).
The intended regime is asymptotic stochastic approximation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The Robbins-Monro calibration \(\sum_t\alpha_t=\infty\) and \(\sum_t\alpha_t^2<\infty\) accumulates descent weight while keeping quadratic noise summable.

notation.meaning: Constant multiplying the quadratic stochastic error

review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Asymptotic stepsize condition for analyses with quadratic accumulated noise.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A diminishing stepsize schedule is calibrated by
\[
\alpha_t>0,
\qquad
\sum_{t=0}^{\infty}\alpha_t=infty,
\qquad
\sum_{t=0}^{\infty}\alpha_t^2<infty.
\]
The first divergence prevents the total descent weight from being finite, while the second condition makes \(\sum_t C\alpha_t^2\) finite. A power schedule \(\alpha_t=a(t+1)^{-p}\), with \(a>0\), satisfies both conditions exactly when \(1/2<p\leq1\). This condition alone does not establish convergence without the corresponding descent estimate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use positive diminishing steps whose sum diverges but whose squared sum converges; power schedules satisfy this when their exponent lies above one-half and at most one.
knowledge_statements.title: Stepsize Calibration

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition content kind fits Stepsize Calibration, and the power-schedule exponent range is standard. However, C<infty and both occurrences of =infty are malformed mathematical text, while the assumed descent estimate is too schematic to identify the applicable weakly convex method. No inspectable source is supplied to resolve that scope.

children.title: Coupled Parameter Regimes
children.top_down_role: Covers admissible combinations of regularization and stepsize choices.

knowledge_statements.title: Coupled Parameter Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Admissible Moreau regularization coupled to stable stochastic envelope-gradient steps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^d\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, and \(\rho\)-weakly convex. For \(0<\lambda<1/\rho\), set \(L_\lambda=\max\{\lambda^{-1},\rho/(1-\rho\lambda)\}\). A regularization-stepsize pair \((\lambda,\eta)\) is in the coupled stable regime when \[0<\lambda<1/\rho,\qquad 0<\eta\le L_\lambda^{-1}.\] Thus increasing \(\lambda\) toward \(1/\rho\) forces \(\eta\le(1-\rho\lambda)/\rho\), while small \(\lambda\) forces \(\eta\le\lambda\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The envelope parameter must stay below the weak-convexity threshold, and the stepsize must decrease according to the resulting envelope smoothness bound.
assumptions_latex: The update uses a gradient or unbiased stochastic gradient of \(f_\lambda\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((\lambda,\eta)\) is calibrated by \(0<\eta\le L_\lambda^{-1}\).

notation.meaning: valid Lipschitz bound for the envelope gradient

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The envelope smoothness bound is standard, but the cited weak-convexity section does not yet substantiate calling the stepsize condition stable for an unspecified stochastic update. Stability depends on the update, noise assumptions, and convergence criterion. The case rho=0 also requires either rho>0 or the convention 1/0=+infinity.

children.title: Calibration Sensitivity
children.top_down_role: Covers performance sensitivity to parameter misspecification.

knowledge_statements.title: Calibration Sensitivity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sensitivity of admissible stepsizes near both ends of the Moreau-parameter interval.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\rho>0\). For each \(t\in(0,1/\rho)\), define \(L_t=\max\{t^{-1},\rho/(1-\rho t)\}\). Then \[L_t^{-1}=\min\{t,(1-\rho t)/\rho\},\] and consequently \[\lim_{t\downarrow0}L_t^{-1}=\lim_{t\uparrow1/\rho}L_t^{-1}=0.\] Moreover, if \(1/(2\rho)\le t<1/\rho\) and \(0<\delta<1/\rho-t\), then the upper-threshold branch is active and \[L_{t+\delta}^{-1}=\frac{1-\rho(t+\delta)}{\rho}=L_t^{-1}-\delta.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The calibrated stepsize ceiling tends to zero at both endpoints. On the upper-threshold branch, increasing the envelope parameter by an admissible amount delta decreases the ceiling by exactly delta.
assumptions_latex: For the perturbation identity, \(1/(2\rho)\le t<1/\rho\) and \(0<\delta<1/\rho-t\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_t^{-1}\) tends to zero at both endpoints, and \(L_{t+\delta}^{-1}=L_t^{-1}-\delta\) under the stated upper-branch conditions.

notation.meaning: admissible increase in the envelope parameter

knowledge_statements.title: Stationarity-Certificate Estimation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monte Carlo certification of Moreau-envelope stationarity from an unbiased gradient oracle.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix \(0<\lambda<1/ho\) and a point \(x\). Given conditionally independent vectors \(G_1(x),\ldots,G_m(x)\) satisfying \(\mathbb E[G_i(x)\mid x]=
abla f_\lambda(x)\) and \(\mathbb E[\|G_i(x)-
abla f_\lambda(x)\|^2\mid x]\le\sigma^2\), define \(\widehat g_m(x)=m^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^mG_i(x)\). Then \[\mathbb E[\|\widehat g_m(x)-
abla f_\lambda(x)\|^2\mid x]\le\sigma^2/m.\] Hence \(\|\widehat g_m(x)\|\le\varepsilon-\sigma/\sqrt{m\delta}\) certifies \(\|
abla f_\lambda(x)\|\le\varepsilon\) with conditional probability at least \(1-\delta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A batch average estimates the envelope gradient with mean-square error decreasing as one over batch size and yields a probabilistic stationarity certificate.
assumptions_latex: The oracle vectors are conditionally independent and unbiased.
Their conditional second moments are bounded by \(\sigma^2\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb P(\|\nabla f_\lambda(x)\|\le\varepsilon\mid x)\ge1-\delta\) under the displayed test.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The mean-square estimate and probabilistic test are plausible, but no source is supplied. The objective, ambient space, weak-convexity modulus, positive integer m, and admissible certificate threshold are not fully introduced; a useful displayed test also requires epsilon to be at least sigma/sqrt(m delta).

knowledge_statements.title: Budget-Aware Stopping
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Oracle-budget stopping with randomized output and optional certificate allocation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given an oracle budget \(B\), batch sizes \(m_k\ge1\), stepsizes \(\eta_k>0\), and certificate reserve \(q\ge0\), initialize \(x_0\). Execute iteration \(k\) only when \(\sum_{j=0}^{k}m_j+q\le B\), using exactly \(m_k\) oracle calls to construct the prescribed stochastic update. Let \(K\) be the number executed. Draw \(R\in\{0,\ldots,K-1\}\) with \(\mathbb P(R=k)=\eta_k/\sum_{j=0}^{K-1}\eta_j\), spend at most \(q\) remaining calls estimating stationarity at \(x_R\), and output \((x_R,\widehat g_q(x_R))\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Iterations run only while their batches and reserved certification calls fit the budget; a stepsize-weighted iterate is returned and optionally certified.
assumptions_latex: The update consumes exactly \(m_k\) oracle calls.
At least one iteration fits the budget.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The total number of oracle calls is at most \(B\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source supports this particular stopping and randomized-output algorithm. In addition, the permitted case q=0 leaves the output estimate hat g_q undefined, and the prescribed stochastic update is not specified sufficiently to identify the algorithm.

knowledge_statements.title: Loss of Weak Convexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global failure of finite weak convexity can destroy every Moreau envelope.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\) given by \(f(y)=-y^4\). For every finite \(\rho\ge0\), the function \(y\mapsto f(y)+(\rho/2)y^2\) is nonconvex, so \(f\) is not globally \(\rho\)-weakly convex. Moreover, for every \(\lambda>0\) and \(x\in\mathbb R\), \[\inf_{y\in\mathbb R}\left\{-y^4+\frac{(y-x)^2}{2\lambda}\right\}=-\infty.\] Thus no positive global envelope parameter produces a finite Moreau envelope or a proximal stationarity map.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The function minus the fourth power has no finite global weak-convexity modulus, and its Moreau subproblem is unbounded for every positive parameter.
assumptions_latex: The domain is all of \(\mathbb R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f_\lambda(x)=-\infty\) and \(\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda f}(x)=\varnothing\) for all \(\lambda>0\) and \(x\in\mathbb R\).

children.title: Envelope-Parameter Admissibility
children.top_down_role: Covers parameter ranges supporting the intended envelope geometry.

knowledge_statements.title: Envelope-Parameter Admissibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Parameter interval ensuring a finite differentiable Moreau envelope for weakly convex functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^d\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, and \(\rho\)-weakly convex. A Moreau parameter \(\lambda\) is admissible when \(0<\lambda<1/\rho\), with \(1/0=+\infty\). For every \(x\in\mathbb R^d\), the function \[y\mapsto f(y)+\frac{1}{2\lambda}\|y-x\|^2\] is \((1/\lambda-\rho)\)-strongly convex, has a unique minimizer \(P_\lambda(x)\), and satisfies \(\nabla f_\lambda(x)=\lambda^{-1}(x-P_\lambda(x))\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Moreau parameter below the reciprocal weak-convexity modulus makes every proximal subproblem strongly convex and the envelope differentiable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P_\lambda(x)\) is single-valued and \(\nabla f_\lambda(x)=\lambda^{-1}(x-P_\lambda(x))\).

notation.meaning: proximal mapping of f at parameter lambda

children.title: Proximal-Parameter Thresholds
children.top_down_role: Covers regularization thresholds relevant to stable proximal points.

knowledge_statements.title: Proximal-Parameter Thresholds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharpness of the reciprocal weak-convexity threshold for proximal well-posedness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(f(y)=-(\rho/2)y^2\) on \(\mathbb R\), where \(\rho>0\), the proximal objective is \[f(y)+\frac{(y-x)^2}{2\lambda}=\frac{1-\rho\lambda}{2\lambda}y^2-\frac{x}{\lambda}y+\frac{x^2}{2\lambda}.\] It has a unique minimizer when \(0<\lambda<1/\rho\). At \(\lambda=1/\rho\), it is constant in \(y\) for \(x=0\) and unbounded below for \(x\ne0\); for \(\lambda>1/\rho\), it is unbounded below for every \(x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A concave quadratic shows that the reciprocal weak-convexity threshold is sharp: uniqueness fails at equality and proximal subproblems become unbounded beyond it.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The universal well-posedness range \(0<\lambda<1/\rho\) cannot be enlarged.

children.title: Oversmoothing Regimes
children.top_down_role: Covers parameter choices that obscure meaningful stationarity information.

knowledge_statements.title: Oversmoothing Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Large admissible envelope parameters can attenuate curvature and conceal local scale.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(y)=(\mu/2)y^2\) on \(\mathbb R\), with \(\mu>0\). For every \(\lambda>0\), \[P_\lambda(x)=\frac{x}{1+\lambda\mu},\qquad f_\lambda(x)=\frac{\mu}{2(1+\lambda\mu)}x^2,\qquad \nabla f_\lambda(x)=\frac{\mu}{1+\lambda\mu}x.\] Hence the envelope curvature and gradient magnitude are attenuated by \((1+\lambda\mu)^{-1}\). When \(\lambda\mu\gg1\), envelope-gradient magnitudes can be arbitrarily smaller than those of \(f\), even though both functions have the same unique stationary point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a quadratic objective, a large envelope parameter suppresses curvature and gradient magnitude, potentially making finite-accuracy stationarity tests misleadingly permissive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
\(\|
abla f_\lambda(x)\|/\|
abla f(x)\|=(1+\lambda\mu)^{-1}\) for \(x
e0\).

children.title: Proximal Instability Regimes
children.top_down_role: Covers invalid choices that produce unstable or unusable proximal constructions.

knowledge_statements.title: Proximal Instability Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proximal sensitivity diverges as the admissible parameter approaches its upper threshold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(f(y)=-(\rho/2)y^2\), \(\rho>0\), and \(0<\lambda<1/\rho\), the proximal point is \[P_\lambda(x)=\frac{x}{1-\rho\lambda}.\] Therefore \(P_\lambda\) has Lipschitz modulus \((1-\rho\lambda)^{-1}\), which diverges as \(\lambda\uparrow1/\rho\). An input perturbation \(e\) produces \(|P_\lambda(x+e)-P_\lambda(x)|=|e|/(1-\rho\lambda)\); thus arbitrarily small oracle or arithmetic errors can undergo arbitrarily large amplification near the threshold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Even below the admissibility threshold, proximal points become increasingly sensitive, with perturbation amplification diverging as the parameter approaches the boundary.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{Lip}(P_\lambda)=(1-\rho\lambda)^{-1}\to+\infty\) as \(\lambda\uparrow1/\rho\).

knowledge_statements.title: Nonunique or Unstable Proximal Points
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss of strong proximal curvature permits nonuniqueness and unbounded sensitivity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(y)=-(\rho/2)y^2\) with \(\rho>0\). At \(\lambda=1/\rho\) and \(x=0\), every \(y\in\mathbb R\) minimizes \(f(y)+(2\lambda)^{-1}(y-x)^2\), so \(P_\lambda(0)=\mathbb R\). For \(0<\lambda<1/\rho\), \(P_\lambda(x)=x/(1-\rho\lambda)\), whose Lipschitz modulus diverges at the threshold. Hence loss of strict proximal curvature manifests first as ill-conditioning and then as a set-valued proximal map.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: As proximal strong convexity vanishes, the proximal map becomes arbitrarily ill-conditioned and can become nonunique at the boundary.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Proximal uniqueness and uniform stability fail as \(\lambda\uparrow1/\rho\).

knowledge_statements.title: Loss of Constraint Prox-Regularity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A crossing constraint set lacks locally unique projections at its intersection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C=\{(s,0):s\in\mathbb R\}\cup\{(0,t):t\in\mathbb R\}\subset\mathbb R^2\). For every \(a>0\), the point \(z_a=(a,a)\) has two distinct nearest points in \(C\), namely \((a,0)\) and \((0,a)\), both at distance \(a\). Since \(z_a\to(0,0)\) as \(a\downarrow0\), the metric projection onto \(C\) is not single-valued in any neighborhood of the origin. Consequently, \(C\) is not prox-regular at \((0,0)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The union of two crossing axes has two nearest feasible points arbitrarily close to the crossing, so local projection uniqueness and prox-regularity fail.
assumptions_latex: The ambient space is Euclidean \(\mathbb R^2\).
Projection is defined using Euclidean distance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C\) is not prox-regular at \((0,0)\).

notation.meaning: union of the two coordinate axes

source_refs.source_title: Variational Analysis and Generalized Differentiation I
source_refs.locator: 4.3 Sensitivity Analysis for Constraint Systems p. 406

source_witnesses.source_title: Variational Analysis and Generalized Differentiation I
source_witnesses.locator: 4.3 Sensitivity Analysis for Constraint Systems p. 406

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The crossing-axes projection example is mathematically plausible and the counterexample kind fits the leaf, but the cited sensitivity-analysis locator is indirect and has not been shown to support the precise local projection characterization of prox-regularity used in the conclusion.

knowledge_statements.title: Persistent Oracle Bias
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonvanishing mean oracle bias creates a nonzero true-stationarity floor.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f(x)=x^2/2\) on \(\mathbb R\), and let the oracle return \(G(x,\xi)=x+b+\varepsilon(\xi)\), where \(b
e0\), \(\mathbb E[\varepsilon(\xi)]=0\), and \(\mathbb E[\varepsilon(\xi)^2]<\infty\). Then \(\mathbb E[G(x,\xi)]=
abla f(x)+b\), whose zero is \(x=-b\), not the stationary point \(0\) of \(f\). Any stochastic approximation converging to the mean-oracle root therefore returns a point with true stationarity residual \(|
abla f(-b)|=|b|\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constant nonzero oracle bias shifts the mean-oracle root away from the true optimizer and imposes a stationarity error equal to the bias magnitude.
assumptions_latex: The noise is centered with finite variance.
The method converges to a zero of the mean oracle.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The limiting true-stationarity residual is \(|b|>0\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The additive-bias example is self-contained and correctly identifies the shifted mean-oracle root under the stated convergence assumption, but no citation supports its use as a persistent-oracle-bias failure record.

knowledge_statements.title: Uncontrolled Noise Moments
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of mean-square stochastic-subgradient analysis when conditional noise moments lack a uniform bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G_k\) be a stochastic subgradient sampled at \(x_k\), and let \(\mathcal F_k\) contain the history before sampling. Even if \(\mathbb E[G_k\mid\mathcal F_k]\in\partial f(x_k)\), the usual mean-square recursion is not finite when \(\mathbb E[\|G_k\|^2\mid\mathcal F_k]=\infty\), and it is not uniformly controlled when \(\sup_k\mathbb E[\|G_k\|^2\mid\mathcal F_k]=\infty\). Consequently, the accumulated variance term \(\sum_k\alpha_k^2\mathbb E[\|G_k\|^2\mid\mathcal F_k]\) need not be finite, so convergence and complexity conclusions based on bounded second moments do not follow.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Without finite, uniformly controlled conditional second moments, the variance term in stochastic-subgradient recursions may diverge, invalidating standard convergence and complexity bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sum_k\alpha_k^2\mathbb E[\|G_k\|^2\mid\mathcal F_k]\text{ need not be finite}

notation.meaning: Information available before the kth oracle sample

review_flags: Exact stochastic-oracle moment failure statement lacks a supplied supporting locator.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role fits the leaf, but no source or inspectable locator is supplied. The claim that the accumulated term need not be finite also depends on the stepsize sequence; unbounded conditional second moments alone do not force divergence, so a source and precise quantification are needed.

knowledge_statements.title: Adversarial Sampling Dependence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure caused by samples chosen dependently from the algorithmic history.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G_k=g(x_k,\xi_k)\) and let \(\mathcal F_k\) contain all previous iterates and samples. If the conditional law of \(\xi_k\) may depend adversarially on \(\mathcal F_k\), marginal unbiasedness does not imply conditional unbiasedness. Writing \(b_k=\mathbb E[G_k\mid\mathcal F_k]-v_k\) for some \(v_k\in\partial f(x_k)\), an adversary may maintain \(b_k\ne0\) and align it with the update direction. Then the conditional cross term involving \(b_k\) does not vanish, and convergence results requiring a martingale-difference oracle are inapplicable unless this bias is controlled.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: History-dependent sampling can create persistent conditional bias even when marginal samples appear unbiased, defeating martingale-difference convergence arguments.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathbb E[G_k\mid\mathcal F_k]-v_k=b_k\ne0\text{ may persist}

notation.meaning: Conditional oracle bias relative to a true subgradient

review_flags: No supplied locator addresses adaptive or adversarial sampling dependence.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The content kind and local topic match, but no source supports the adaptive-sampling failure claim. “Marginal unbiasedness” must be defined with respect to a fixed iterate or joint law before its contrast with conditional unbiasedness is mathematically reliable.

knowledge_statements.title: Samplewise Geometry Mismatch
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Population weak convexity does not supply the uniform samplewise curvature required by model-based updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F(x)=\mathbb E[f(x,\xi)]\) be \(\rho\)-weakly convex. This population property alone does not imply that \(f(\cdot,\xi)\) is \(\rho\)-weakly convex almost surely, or even weakly convex with an integrable random modulus. Therefore a method whose sampled model requires \(f(\cdot,\xi)+(\rho/2)\|\cdot\|^2\) to be convex cannot infer model convexity from weak convexity of \(F\). Sample proximal subproblems may consequently be nonconvex or unbounded despite well-behaved population geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weak convexity of the expected objective need not hold samplewise; sampled models or proximal subproblems can therefore lose their required geometry.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f(\cdot,\xi)+(\rho/2)\|\cdot\|^2\text{ need not be convex almost surely}
review_flags: Supplied stochastic value-function locator does not establish the samplewise-versus-population failure claim.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Population weak convexity indeed need not imply samplewise weak convexity, and the failure-boundary kind fits. However, no source is supplied, and loss of samplewise weak convexity alone does not establish that a sampled proximal subproblem is unbounded; that stronger possibility requires a construction or supporting locator.

knowledge_statements.title: Uncontrolled Model Error
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Model-based descent fails when approximation error is not controlled relative to the trial displacement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a model \(m_x\) of \(f\) at \(x\), define \(e_x(y)=f(y)-m_x(y)\). Model-based descent analyses commonly require a bound such as \(|e_x(y)|\le(\omega/2)\|y-x\|^2\) locally, with deterministic or integrably controlled \(\omega\). If no such modulus exists, or if \(|e_x(y_k)|/\|y_k-x_k\|^2\) is unbounded along computed trial points, predicted model decrease need not imply actual objective decrease. Thus neither a descent recursion nor a stationarity bound derived from model accuracy is justified.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If model error is unbounded relative to squared step length, predicted decrease may not transfer to the true objective.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sup_k\frac{|e_{x_k}(y_k)|}{\|y_k-x_k\|^2}=\infty\Longrightarrow\text{model decrease need not imply objective decrease}
review_flags: The supplied locators do not document this precise model-accuracy failure boundary.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record fits the failure leaf, but no source is supplied. The claimed transfer failure depends on the precise predicted-decrease condition, model construction, and accepted trial rule, none of which is defined sufficiently to validate the stated boundary.

knowledge_statements.title: Insufficient Model Regularization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp proximal-parameter boundary for a weakly convex model subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m_x\) be \(\rho\)-weakly convex and consider \(q_x(y)=m_x(y)+(2\eta)^{-1}\|y-x\|^2\). The function \(q_x\) is \((\eta^{-1}-\rho)\)-strongly convex only when \(0<\eta<\rho^{-1}\). At \(\eta=\rho^{-1}\), uniqueness can fail. For \(\eta>\rho^{-1}\), even the model \(m_x(y)=-(\rho/2)\|y\|^2\) makes \(q_0(y)=((\eta^{-1}-\rho)/2)\|y\|^2\) unbounded below. Hence regularization at or below the curvature modulus cannot guarantee a unique, well-posed model step.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A rho-weakly convex model requires proximal curvature strictly exceeding rho; equality loses strong convexity, while weaker regularization may yield an unbounded subproblem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \eta<\rho^{-1}\text{ is required for guaranteed strong convexity of }q_x

knowledge_statements.title: Dominant Subproblem Inexactness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Outer stationarity guarantees fail when inner-solve errors do not decay sufficiently.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(q_k\) be a \(\mu_k\)-strongly convex proximal-model objective with minimizer \(y_k^\star\), and suppose the computed point satisfies \(q_k(y_k)\le q_k(y_k^\star)+\delta_k\). Strong convexity gives \(\|y_k-y_k^\star\|\le\sqrt{2\delta_k/\mu_k}\). For the residual \(r_k=\eta_k^{-1}(x_k-y_k)\), its deviation from the exact residual can therefore be as large as \(\eta_k^{-1}\sqrt{2\delta_k/\mu_k}\). If this quantity does not vanish at the requested stationarity scale, the subproblem error dominates and the computed residual cannot certify that scale.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An inner objective gap produces residual error proportional to its square root; if that error exceeds the target tolerance, outer stationarity is uncertified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \|r_k-r_k^\star\|\le\eta_k^{-1}\sqrt{2\delta_k/\mu_k}
review_flags: No supplied locator supports the inexact proximal-residual propagation formula.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The strong-convexity distance estimate and induced residual bound are mathematically standard, and the failure-boundary role fits. No supporting source is supplied, however, and the exact residual r_k^star used in the conclusion is not introduced in the statement or notation.

knowledge_statements.title: Prohibitive Proximal-Subproblem Cost
knowledge_statements.scope_note: End-to-end efficiency requires explicit control of each proximal subproblem's computational cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose an outer method needs \(N(\varepsilon)\) proximal-model steps to produce an \(\varepsilon\)-stationary output, and step \(k\) requires \(T_k(\delta_k)\) primitive oracle calls to reach inner tolerance \(\delta_k\). Its total primitive-oracle cost is \(\sum_{k=0}^{N(\varepsilon)-1}T_k(\delta_k)\). An outer iteration bound alone is not an implementable complexity guarantee when these inner costs are unbounded, unavailable, or super-polynomial in \(1/\delta_k\). In that regime, exact-proximal-oracle complexity does not imply tractability in the underlying computational model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An outer iteration bound is not an end-to-end complexity guarantee when proximal subproblems have uncontrolled or prohibitive primitive-oracle cost.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T_{\mathrm{total}}(\varepsilon)=\sum_{k=0}^{N(\varepsilon)-1}T_k(\delta_k)

notation.meaning: Primitive cost of the kth inner solve

review_flags: The supplied proximal-method locator does not establish this nested-complexity boundary.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The nested-cost accounting matches the terminal failure container, but no source is supplied. “Super-polynomial” and “tractability” require an explicitly stated input-size and primitive-oracle computational model before the boundary is a precise complexity claim.

knowledge_statements.title: Dimension-Driven Query Degradation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A concrete variance barrier for one-point random-direction gradient estimation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=\langle a,x\rangle\) on \(\mathbb R^d\), let \(u\) be uniform on the unit sphere, and use the one-point estimator \(G=d\bigl(f(x+\mu u)-f(x)\bigr)u/\mu=d\langle a,u\rangle u\). Then \(\mathbb E[G]=a\), but \(\mathbb E\|G\|^2=d\|a\|^2\), so \(\mathbb E\|G-a\|^2=(d-1)\|a\|^2\). Thus the estimator's variance grows linearly with dimension even for a linear objective, precluding dimension-free query bounds for methods relying on this estimator without additional structure or variance reduction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The standard one-point spherical estimator has variance linear in dimension even on linear objectives, preventing dimension-free query complexity without extra structure.
review_flags: Exact random-direction variance identity lacks a supplied supporting source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The estimator identities are correct for a uniform spherical direction and the failure-boundary role fits, but the exact variance identity and resulting query-complexity limitation have no supplied source or locator.

knowledge_statements.title: Raw-Subgradient Norm Instability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Raw selected-subgradient norms need not reflect nonsmooth stationarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the convex function \(f(x)=|x|\), every \(x\ne0\) has the unique subgradient \(g(x)=\operatorname{sign}(x)\), hence \(\|g(x)\|=1\) even as \(x\to0\), while \(0\) is the minimizer. Moreover, \(\partial f(0)=[-1,1]\): a valid oracle may return \(g=1\) at the stationary point although \(0\in\partial f(0)\). Therefore the norm of an arbitrarily selected raw subgradient is discontinuous near stationarity and is not, by itself, a valid stationarity certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For absolute value, raw subgradients can retain norm one arbitrarily near—and even at—the minimizer, so their selected norm is not a reliable certificate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: 0\in\partial f(0)\text{ while a valid selected }g\in\partial f(0)\text{ may satisfy }\|g\|=1

notation.meaning: Convex subdifferential of f at x

review_flags: Confirm that the cited section explicitly supports the subdifferential convention used.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The counterexample is correct and counterexample is the appropriate kind, but the cited weak-convexity section is not a sufficiently specific locator for the absolute-value subdifferential facts or the selected-subgradient certificate failure.

children.title: Objective-Value Accuracy
children.top_down_role: Interpretive limits of objective-value accuracy within weakly convex stochastic guarantees.

knowledge_statements.title: Objective-Value Accuracy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global additive objective-gap certificate for a finite-infimum minimization problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:X\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) satisfy \(f_\star=\inf_{z\in X}f(z)>-\infty\). A point \(x\in\operatorname{dom}f\) is globally \(\varepsilon\)-accurate in objective value when \(f(x)-f_\star\le\varepsilon\), where \(\varepsilon\ge0\). If a verifiable lower bound \(L\le f_\star\) is available, the computable inequality \(f(x)-L\le\varepsilon\) certifies this property. Objective-value accuracy alone imposes no stated bound on any subgradient or stationarity residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A point is epsilon-accurate when its objective gap is at most epsilon; a valid lower bound makes the certificate directly checkable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f(x)-f_\star\le\varepsilon

notation.meaning: Verifiable lower bound on the optimum value

source_refs.locator: 5.3 Value Functions Associated with Convex Functions p. 268

review_flags: Confirm that the cited section states the objective-gap convention.

source_witnesses.locator: 5.3 Value Functions Associated with Convex Functions p. 268

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate definition and lower-bound implication are correct and fit the leaf, but the cited section on convex value functions does not specifically locate the global epsilon-objective-gap convention or the claimed lack of a stationarity implication.

children.title: Stationarity Certification
children.top_down_role: Stationarity-focused certificate interpretation for nonsmooth weakly convex objectives.

knowledge_statements.title: Stationarity Certification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Moreau-envelope stationarity certificate for finite-dimensional weakly convex objectives, using the limiting subdifferential.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, and \(\rho\)-weakly convex, and let \(\partial f\) denote the limiting subdifferential. For \(0<\lambda<\rho^{-1}\), define \(x^+=\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda f}(x)\). The proximal point is unique, the Moreau envelope \(f_\lambda\) is differentiable, and \(\nabla f_\lambda(x)=\lambda^{-1}(x-x^+)\in\partial f(x^+)\). Hence \(\lambda^{-1}\|x-x^+\|\le\varepsilon\) certifies both \(\|\nabla f_\lambda(x)\|\le\varepsilon\) and \(\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(x^+))\le\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a proper lower-semicontinuous weakly convex objective, a small proximal residual certifies a small Moreau-envelope gradient at the query point and a small limiting-subgradient residual at its proximal point.
assumptions_latex: f:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\text{ is proper, lower semicontinuous, and }\rho\text{-weakly convex}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \lambda^{-1}\|x-x^+\|\le\varepsilon\Longrightarrow \|\nabla f_\lambda(x)\|\le\varepsilon\text{ and }\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(x^+))\le\varepsilon

notation.meaning: Unique proximal point of x with parameter lambda

children.title: Accuracy–Stationarity Nonimplication
children.top_down_role: Cases where objective-value quality does not support the intended stationarity conclusion.

knowledge_statements.title: Accuracy–Stationarity Nonimplication
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Objective accuracy does not uniformly imply small nonsmooth stationarity residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(M>0\) and let \(f_M(x)=M|x|\) on \(\mathbb R\). Its minimum value is \(0\) at \(x=0\). For every \(\varepsilon>0\), the point \(x_\varepsilon=\varepsilon/M\) satisfies \(f_M(x_\varepsilon)-\inf f_M=\varepsilon\), but \(\partial f_M(x_\varepsilon)=\{M\}\), so \(\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f_M(x_\varepsilon))=M\). Since \(M\) is arbitrary, no universal bound tending to zero with the objective gap can control the raw subgradient stationarity residual over convex, hence weakly convex, objectives.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scaled absolute-value functions have arbitrarily small objective gaps at points whose subgradient residual remains arbitrarily large, disproving accuracy-to-stationarity implication.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f_M(x_\varepsilon)-\inf f_M=\varepsilon\quad\text{and}\quad\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f_M(x_\varepsilon))=M
review_flags: Confirm that the cited section supports the subdifferential facts underlying the explicit counterexample.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The scaled absolute-value counterexample is correct and its content kind exactly fits the nonimplication leaf. The cited weak-convexity section, however, does not specifically locate the absolute-value subdifferential calculation or the asserted universal nonimplication boundary.

children.title: Certificate-Strength Mismatch
children.top_down_role: Overclaims caused by treating objective accuracy as a stronger stationarity certificate.

knowledge_statements.title: Certificate-Strength Mismatch
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete separation between objective-value accuracy and stationarity for a smooth, hence weakly convex, objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f_a:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\) be defined by \(f_a(x)=a x^2\), where \(a>0\), and let \(f_a^*=0\). For any prescribed \(\varepsilon>0\) and \(M>0\), choose \(a>M^2/(4\varepsilon)\) and \(x=\sqrt{\varepsilon/a}\). Then \(f_a(x)-f_a^*=\varepsilon\), while \(\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f_a(x))=|2ax|=2\sqrt{a\varepsilon}>M\). Thus an \(\varepsilon\)-objective-gap certificate alone yields no uniform stationarity certificate over weakly convex objectives without additional regularity controlling objective growth or slope.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Arbitrarily accurate objective values can coexist with arbitrarily large stationarity residuals across weakly convex objectives, so value accuracy alone is not a stationarity certificate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f_a(x)-f_a^*=\varepsilon\quad\text{and}\quad\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f_a(x))>M\).

notation.meaning: limiting subdifferential of f at x

review_flags: exact counterexample is self-contained but lacks an authoritative supplied locator

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The counterexample is mathematically correct, self-contained, and appropriately classified as a failure boundary, but no inspectable source locator supports the accuracy-stationarity separation claim.

knowledge_statements.title: Iterate-Selection Bias
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of transferring per-iterate stochastic guarantees to data-dependent output selection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Z_1,\ldots,Z_T\) be nonnegative random stationarity residuals with \(\mathbb E[Z_t]\leq\varepsilon\) for every deterministic \(t\). For an output index \(\tau\) chosen using the observed trajectory, these inequalities do not imply \(\mathbb E[Z_\tau]\leq\varepsilon\). Indeed, if the \(Z_t\) are independent with \(\mathbb P(Z_t=1)=\varepsilon\) and \(\mathbb P(Z_t=0)=1-\varepsilon\), and \(\tau\) selects an index attaining the maximum, then \(\mathbb E[Z_\tau]=1-(1-\varepsilon)^T\), which can greatly exceed \(\varepsilon\). Independence of \(\tau\) from the certification samples or a selection-adjusted analysis is therefore required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bounds for fixed iterates need not survive trajectory-dependent selection; choosing the largest observed residual raises its expectation from ε to one minus (1−ε)^T.
assumptions_latex: \(Z_1,\ldots,Z_T\) are independent Bernoulli random variables with mean \(\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E[Z_\tau]=1-(1-\varepsilon)^T>\varepsilon\) for \(\tau\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{1\leq t\leq T}Z_t\).

notation.meaning: nonnegative residual or failure indicator at iterate t

review_flags: self-contained probability counterexample lacks a supplied supporting locator
selection protocol must be matched to the intended algorithmic theorem

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Bernoulli maximum example correctly shows that fixed-index expectation bounds need not transfer to trajectory-dependent selection. A source is still required, especially for the concluding prescription about certification independence or selection-adjusted analysis.

knowledge_statements.title: Expectation-Only Guarantee Misinterpretation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Expectation bounds do not automatically provide same-threshold high-probability or pathwise certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Z\geq0\) be a random stationarity residual satisfying only \(\mathbb E[Z]\leq\varepsilon\). Markov's inequality yields \(\mathbb P(Z>\varepsilon/\delta)\leq\delta\) for every \(\delta\in(0,1)\), but it does not yield \(\mathbb P(Z\leq\varepsilon)\geq1-\delta\). For example, if \(Z=1\) with probability \(\varepsilon\) and \(Z=0\) otherwise, where \(0<\varepsilon<1\), then \(\mathbb E[Z]=\varepsilon\) but \(\mathbb P(Z>\varepsilon)=\varepsilon\). Converting expectation guarantees into sharper tail guarantees requires additional concentration assumptions, repetitions, or a larger certification threshold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An expected residual of ε only gives a threshold ε/δ with confidence 1−δ; it does not certify residual at most ε with arbitrary high confidence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb P(Z>\varepsilon/\delta)\leq\delta\), while no same-threshold \((1-\delta)\)-confidence conclusion follows in general.
review_flags: standard Markov-inequality argument lacks an authoritative supplied locator

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Markov inequality statement and counterexample are correct, and failure_boundary fits the leaf. No authoritative section, theorem, or page locator is supplied.

children.title: Finite-Sum Variance Reduction
children.top_down_role: Only weakly convex specializations and comparative rates belong here; the general method families belong to the variance-reduction chapter.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Sum Variance Reduction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weakly convex finite-sum specialization; general variance-reduction method families remain outside this chapter.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(F(x)=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n f_i(x)+r(x)\) on \(\mathbb R^d\), where each \(f_i\) is \(\rho_i\)-weakly convex and \(r\) is proper, closed, and convex. Then \(F\) is \(\bar\rho\)-weakly convex for \(\bar\rho=n^{-1}\sum_i\rho_i\). Given a reference point \(\widetilde x\), a variance-reduced component estimator has the control-variate form \(v(x;i)=g_i(x)-g_i(\widetilde x)+\bar g(\widetilde x)\), where \(g_i(y)\) is a measurable component oracle and \(\bar g(y)=n^{-1}\sum_j g_j(y)\). Uniform sampling gives \(\mathbb E_i[v(x;i)]=\bar g(x)\); usefulness additionally requires control of its second moment.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A weakly convex finite sum remains weakly convex, and a component-oracle control variate is unbiased while potentially reducing variance near its reference point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\text{ is }\bar\rho\text{-weakly convex}\quad\text{and}\quad\mathbb E_i[v(x;i)]=\bar g(x)\).
review_flags: variance-reduction representation needs a method-specific source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cited weak-convexity section can plausibly support closure of weak convexity under averaging, but it does not support the control-variate representation or its variance-reduction interpretation. A method-specific source is required, and it should establish that the material is a weakly convex specialization rather than a generic variance-reduction method family.

children.title: Distributed-Federated Coordination Taxonomy

children.title: Distributed Weakly Convex Optimization
children.top_down_role: Distributed formulations whose primary structure is network-coupled optimization.

knowledge_statements.title: Distributed Weakly Convex Optimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Problem-class definition separating weak convexity from the choice of distributed coordination protocol.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A distributed weakly convex optimization problem consists of agents \(i=1,\ldots,m\) with local objectives \(F_i:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) and the global objective \(F(x)=m^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^m F_i(x)\). Each \(F_i\) is \(\rho_i\)-weakly convex when \(F_i+(\rho_i/2)\|\cdot\|^2\) is convex. Consequently, \(F\) is \(\bar\rho\)-weakly convex for \(\bar\rho=m^{-1}\sum_i\rho_i\). Computation is distributed when agent \(i\) accesses only its local oracle and coordination communicates information sufficient to approximate a common decision or aggregate update.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Agents own local weakly convex objectives whose average is weakly convex; a distributed method combines local oracle work with communication toward a common decision.
assumptions_latex: \(F_i\) is proper and \(\rho_i\)-weakly convex for each agent \(i\).
All local decisions lie in the common space \(\mathbb R^d\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F=m^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^mF_i\text{ is }\bar\rho\text{-weakly convex},\qquad\bar\rho=m^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^m\rho_i\).
review_flags: distributed problem-class definition needs a coordination-specific source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The averaging calculation is correct and definition is a suitable role for this problem-class leaf. The cited weak-convexity section does not support the distributed-oracle and communication characterization.

children.title: Federated Weakly Convex Optimization
children.top_down_role: Federated formulations centered on client heterogeneity, partial participation, or privacy constraints.

assumptions_latex: Clients retain local oracle access to their own objectives.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\text{ is }\rho_F\text{-weakly convex},\qquad\rho_F=\sum_{i=1}^m p_i\rho_i\).

notation.meaning: private local objective of client i

review_flags: federated protocol definition needs a federated-optimization source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Client-population formulation with heterogeneous local data and partial client participation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A federated weakly convex problem minimizes \(F(x)=\sum_{i=1}^m p_iF_i(x)\), where \(p_i\geq0\), \(\sum_i p_i=1\), and client \(i\) evaluates an oracle for its private local objective \(F_i\). If \(F_i\) is \(\rho_i\)-weakly convex, then \(F\) is \(\rho_F\)-weakly convex with \(\rho_F=\sum_i p_i\rho_i\). A federated protocol selects a possibly random client subset each round, performs local oracle steps, and aggregates communicated client updates at a coordinating server; heterogeneity and participation sampling are therefore part of its stochastic oracle model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Federated weakly convex optimization averages private client objectives and uses sampled client participation, local computation, and server aggregation under possible data heterogeneity.
knowledge_statements.title: Federated Weakly Convex Optimization

children.title: Network-Coupled Coordination
children.top_down_role: Communication topology, consensus effects, and coordination burdens delegated to distributed-optimization coverage.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((I-W)X=0\iff X=\mathbf1\bar x^{\mathsf T}\), and repeated mixing contracts the disagreement component.
review_flags: network mixing and consensus conditions lack a supplied distributed-optimization locator
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consensus feasibility and mixing conditions for peer-to-peer coordination over a communication graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let each agent hold \(x_i\in\mathbb R^d\), and stack the rows in \(X\in\mathbb R^{m\times d}\). Exact network consensus is the condition \(X=\mathbf 1\bar x^{\mathsf T}\) for some \(\bar x\in\mathbb R^d\), equivalently \((I-W)X=0\), provided the mixing matrix \(W\in\mathbb R^{m\times m}\) is compatible with the communication graph, satisfies \(W\mathbf1=\mathbf1\) and \(\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}W=\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}\), and has \(\ker(I-W)=\operatorname{span}\{\mathbf1\}\). Repeated mixing contracts disagreement when the restriction of \(W\) to \(\mathbf1^\perp\) has operator norm strictly below one.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Peer-to-peer coordination enforces consensus through a graph-compatible mixing matrix whose nonconsensus modes contract strictly.
knowledge_statements.title: Network-Coupled Coordination

children.title: Client-Server Coordination
children.top_down_role: Server aggregation, client participation, and communication-round analysis delegated to federated-optimization coverage.

knowledge_statements.title: Client-Server Coordination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract synchronous server aggregation pattern, independent of any particular local weakly convex solver.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input weights \(p_i\geq0\), an initial server model \(x^0\in\mathbb R^d\), and rounds \(t=0,\ldots,T-1\). At round \(t\), the server samples a nonempty client set \(S_t\), broadcasts \(x^t\), and each selected client returns an update \(u_i^t\) computed from its local stochastic oracle initialized at \(x^t\). The server chooses aggregation weights \(a_{i,t}\geq0\) satisfying \(\sum_{i\in S_t}a_{i,t}=1\) and sets \(x^{t+1}=x^t+\sum_{i\in S_t}a_{i,t}u_i^t\). Output \(x^T\), or a separately specified randomized iterate when required by the stationarity analysis.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A server broadcasts a model, selected clients compute local updates, and the server forms a normalized weighted aggregate; the output rule must match the analysis.
assumptions_latex: Each returned \(u_i^t\) uses only the broadcast model and client-local information.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^{t+1}=x^t+\sum_{i\in S_t}a_{i,t}u_i^t\), with output \(x^T\) or an analysis-specified randomized iterate.
review_flags: abstract coordination algorithm lacks a supplied federated or distributed source
local update rule intentionally unspecified at this taxonomy boundary

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind correctly reflects the terminal container, and the abstract update is internally consistent. No source supports this client-server protocol, its weighting convention, or the output-rule qualification.

children.title: Weakly-Convex–Concave Minimax Optimization
children.top_down_role: Primal-dual algorithms, saddle envelopes, and game complexity belong to the minimax chapter.

knowledge_statements.title: Weakly-Convex–Concave Minimax Optimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Problem-class interface only; primal-dual algorithms and game complexity belong to the minimax chapter.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A weakly-convex–concave minimax problem has the form \(\min_{x\in X}\max_{y\in Y}\Phi(x,y)\), where \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) and \(Y\subseteq\mathbb R^q\) are nonempty convex sets. For every \(y\in Y\), the map \(x\mapsto\Phi(x,y)\) is \(\rho\)-weakly convex on \(X\); for every \(x\in X\), the map \(y\mapsto\Phi(x,y)\) is concave on \(Y\). When the inner maximum is attained, the primal value function is \(P(x)=\max_{y\in Y}\Phi(x,y)\); as a pointwise supremum of uniformly \(\rho\)-weakly convex functions, \(P\) is \(\rho\)-weakly convex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The payoff is uniformly weakly convex in the minimizing variable and concave in the maximizing variable; its attained primal value remains weakly convex.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) and \(Y\) are nonempty convex subsets of finite-dimensional Euclidean spaces.
\(\Phi(\cdot,y)\) is uniformly \(\rho\)-weakly convex for all \(y\in Y\).
\(\Phi(x,\cdot)\) is concave and attains its maximum on \(Y\) for every \(x\in X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P(x)=\max_{y\in Y}\Phi(x,y)\text{ is }\rho\text{-weakly convex on }X\).
review_flags: confirm that the cited implicit convex-concave section supports the chosen minimax formulation

children.title: Sample-Average Approximation
children.top_down_role: Empirical approximation structure delegated to stochastic-programming coverage.

assumptions_latex: \(f(\cdot,\xi_i)\) is \(\rho(\xi_i)\)-weakly convex for each realized sample.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F_n(x)=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n f(x,\xi_i)+r(x)\text{ is }\rho_n\text{-weakly convex}\).
review_flags: sample-average definition needs a stochastic-programming source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Empirical finite-sample replacement of an expected weakly convex objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\xi_1,\ldots,\xi_n\) be independent samples from a distribution \(P\), and let \(f:\mathbb R^d\times\Xi\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) be measurable. For the population objective \(F(x)=\mathbb E_P[f(x,\xi)]+r(x)\), its sample-average approximation is \(F_n(x)=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n f(x,\xi_i)+r(x)\). If \(f(\cdot,\xi)\) is \(\rho(\xi)\)-weakly convex and \(r\) is convex, then, for the realized sample, \(F_n\) is \(\rho_n\)-weakly convex with \(\rho_n=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n\rho(\xi_i)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sample-average approximation replaces the population expectation by an empirical mean; its realized weak-convexity modulus is the average of the sample moduli.
knowledge_statements.title: Sample-Average Approximation

children.title: Estimator Consistency
children.top_down_role: Consistency questions for empirical estimators delegated to statistical-estimation coverage.

knowledge_statements.title: Estimator Consistency
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform consistency criterion for sample-average objective-value estimators on a fixed compact decision set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\subset\mathbb R^d\) be compact, \(F(x)=\mathbb E[f(x,\xi)]+r(x)\), and \(F_n(x)=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n f(x,\xi_i)+r(x)\). The sample-average estimator is uniformly strongly consistent on \(K\) when \(\sup_{x\in K}|F_n(x)-F(x)|\to0\) almost surely as \(n\to\infty\). A standard sufficient regime is that \(f(\cdot,\xi)\) is almost surely continuous on \(K\) and dominated there by an integrable envelope; under an applicable uniform law of large numbers, the displayed convergence follows.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The estimator is uniformly strongly consistent when its empirical objective converges almost surely to the population objective uniformly over a compact decision set.
assumptions_latex: The samples \(\xi_i\) are independent with the population law.
A uniform law of large numbers applies to \(\{f(x,\cdot):x\in K\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sup_{x\in K}|F_n(x)-F(x)|\longrightarrow0\quad\text{almost surely}\).
review_flags: uniform-law hypotheses require a stochastic-programming or empirical-process source
supplied locators do not support estimator consistency

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed convergence is a valid definition of uniform strong consistency and property fits the leaf. The asserted sufficient continuity-and-envelope regime and its measurability qualifications require an authoritative uniform-law or stochastic-programming locator.

children.title: Stationary-Solution Consistency

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0\in\partial F(\bar x)\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Outer-limit consistency of approximate stationary points under graphical convergence of sample subdifferentials.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F_n,F:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) be proper lower-semicontinuous functions, and let \(x_n\) satisfy \(\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial F_n(x_n))\leq\varepsilon_n\), where \(\varepsilon_n\to0\). Suppose \(x_n\to\bar x\), and assume the outer graphical consistency condition: whenever \(z_n\to z\), \(v_n\to v\), and \(v_n\in\partial F_n(z_n)\), one has \(v\in\partial F(z)\). Choosing \(v_n\in\partial F_n(x_n)\) with \(\|v_n\|\leq\varepsilon_n+o(1)\) then implies \(0\in\partial F(\bar x)\). Thus every convergent cluster sequence of approximate sample-stationary points is population-stationary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If sample subdifferential graphs have the correct outer limit, every limit of increasingly accurate sample-stationary points is stationary for the population objective.
knowledge_statements.title: Stationary-Solution Consistency

\(n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^n\psi(\bar x;\xi_i)\Rightarrow N(0,\Sigma)\), and the estimating-equation remainder is \(o_p(n^{-1/2})\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sqrt n(\widehat x_n-\bar x)\Rightarrow N(0,A^{-1}\Sigma A^{-\mathsf T})\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local Z-estimator form for a consistent stationary solution; nonsmooth applications require a valid local estimating-map reduction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\xi_1,\ldots,\xi_n\) be i.i.d., and let \(\widehat x_n\in\mathbb R^d\) be a consistent sample-average stationary estimator of \(\bar x\). Suppose a measurable map \(\psi:\mathbb R^d\times\Xi\to\mathbb R^d\) gives the local stationarity representation \[0=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\psi(\widehat x_n;\xi_i)+o_p(n^{-1/2}).\] If the stated differentiability, nonsingularity, and central-limit assumptions hold, then \[\sqrt n(\widehat x_n-\bar x)\Rightarrow N\!\left(0,A^{-1}\Sigma A^{-\mathsf T}\right).\] Thus consistency alone is insufficient: an asymptotic distribution additionally requires a regular local stationarity representation and a nonsingular population linearization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A consistent stationary estimator is asymptotically normal when its local estimating equation has a nonsingular population derivative, a central limit theorem, and negligible remainder.

knowledge_statements.title: Application-Specific Case Studies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Composite-model admission condition for application examples; naming an application alone does not establish weak convexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An application-specific loss is admitted to the stochastic weakly convex framework when it has the composite form \(f_\xi(x)=h_\xi(c_\xi(x))\) under uniform constants \(L\) and \(\beta\). If \(h_\xi\) is convex and globally \(L\)-Lipschitz and the Jacobian of \(c_\xi\) is \(\beta\)-Lipschitz, then \[x\longmapsto f_\xi(x)+\frac{L\beta}{2}\lVert x\rVert^2\] is convex for almost every \(\xi\). Moreover, \[x\longmapsto F(x)+\frac{L\beta}{2}\lVert x\rVert^2\] is convex when \(F(x)=\mathbb E[f_\xi(x)]\) is finite. Phase retrieval, inverse problems, matrix factorization, and learning losses qualify only after their concrete loss and model maps satisfy these hypotheses.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An application is an admissible case study when, with uniform constants, its loss is a globally Lipschitz convex function composed with a smooth map having Lipschitz Jacobian, and its population expectation is finite.
assumptions_latex: For almost every \(\xi\), \(c_\xi:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R^m\) is continuously differentiable and its Jacobian is \(\beta\)-Lipschitz.
For almost every \(\xi\), \(h_\xi:\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R\) is convex and globally \(L\)-Lipschitz.
The constants \(L\) and \(\beta\) are uniform in \(\xi\), and \(F(x)=\mathbb E[h_\xi(c_\xi(x))]\) is finite for every \(x\in\mathbb R^d\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f_\xi=h_\xi\circ c_\xi\) is \(L\beta\)-weakly convex for almost every \(\xi\), and \(F=\mathbb E[f_\xi]\) is \(L\beta\)-weakly convex.

notation.meaning: Smooth application-specific prediction or residual map.
